item.title: ARTA: Graph Combinatorial Optimization for Robust Interbeat Interval Estimation from Wearable Electrocardiogram Signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.00011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate heart rate (HR) and interbeat interval (IBI) estimation from wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) is essential for continuous physiological monitoring, but motion artifacts can create false QRS-like peaks and obscure true R-peaks. Conventional detectors and local interval-repair rules process detections independently and may become unreliable when several consecutive beats are corrupted. We present ARTA (Artifact-Robust Temporal Alignment), a graph-based combinatorial framework that estimates the heartbeat sequence through constrained temporal optimization. ARTA combines candidates from multiple ECG detectors, represents them as nodes in a directed acyclic graph and connects candidates through physiologically plausible RR intervals. Candidate confidence uses detector agreement and local ECG quality, while history-dependent transition costs capture recent IBI consistency and a soft heart-rate prior. Beam-search dynamic programming selects a coherent low-cost path across the recording, suppressing false detections and recovering missed beats when plausible auxiliary candidates are available. On the IEEE Signal Processing Cup exercise dataset with electrode-motion artifacts from -2 to 12 dB, ARTA achieved an HR mean absolute error of 1.79 beats per minute, 54% lower than the strongest single-detector baseline, with 92.38% of windows within +/-5 beats per minute, an R-peak F1 score of 0.95, and an IBI mean absolute error of 6.52 ms. Cross-dataset evaluation on the European ST-T Database further assessed transfer to long clinical ambulatory recordings and a label-free reliability analysis examined conditional performance without using reference annotations for segment selection. ARTA is single-channel, training-free, interpretable and computationally lightweight, operating approximately 27 times faster than real time with peak memory below 2.1 MB in a single-thread CPU simulation.
item.dc:creator: Shovito Barua Soumma, Asiful Arefeen, Hassan Ghasemzadeh

item.title: Dataset and Experimental Testbed for Deep Learning-Based Bluetooth Device Fingerprinting
item.description: arXiv:2611.00332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-enabled wireless networks have emerged as vital components of future-generation wireless communication systems. Among various wireless architectures, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) networks have attracted significant research interest due to their widespread adoption and low cost. In these networks, deep learning (DL) models can be integrated directly into the physical-layer infrastructure to perform diverse tasks, including environment sensing, localization, radio frequency fingerprinting (RFFP), and signal denoising. While highly effective under their original training configurations, these DL models often fail significantly when deployed in unseen environments---such as different rooms, varying temperature conditions, or altered carrier frequencies. Addressing this limitation requires rigorous benchmarking of models and algorithms against unseen configurations to evaluate their generalization and robustness. To bridge this gap, this paper makes two key contributions: i) we introduce a comprehensive, large-scale wireless BLE dataset consisting of raw IQ transmissions from 31 distinct commercial devices captured across diverse days, locations, environments, temperatures, receiver hardware, and frequency channels; ii) we present a case study evaluating state-of-the-art techniques for domain-robust RFFP to advance real-world AI reliability.
item.dc:creator: Haytham Albousayri, Bechir Hamdaoui

item.title: Wideband Channel Measurements in the Lower FR3 Band (6-12 GHz) for Industrial Environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.00426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The upper mid-band, also known as Frequency Range 3 (FR3), spans 7.125-24.25 GHz and is a key candidate band for sixth-generation (6G) wireless communications. However, channel measurements in industrial environments remain scarce, and the 3GPP indoor-factory (InF) channel model, developed for omnidirectional antennas, has yet to be validated across the FR3 band. This paper presents a wideband channel measurement campaign in an industrial production hall, covering 135 line-of-sight (LOS) positions at 1-18 m and 30 non-line-of-sight (NLOS) positions behind an industrial robot at 2.5-16.5 m across 6-12 GHz. In LOS, the path-loss exponent ranged from 1.87 to 2.12, and the close-in fits agreed with the 3GPP InF-LOS model to within approximately 2 dB. However, shadow fading was only 1.4-1.7 dB, compared with the model's 4.3 dB. In NLOS, the robot caused an excess loss that increased from 10.3 to 13.0 dB between 6.5 and 11.5 GHz, consistent with diffraction. Blocking the direct path raised the mean directional delay spread from approximately 5 to 25 ns, close to omnidirectional values. These results indicate that the 3GPP InF model captures mean LOS path loss well but overestimates the variability of beam-aligned FR3 links, and that blockage loss in FR3 is frequency dependent. The dataset and processing code are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Faizan Rauf, Adam Umra, Oways Alsoloh, Aydin Sezgin

item.title: Sense Less, Miss Less: Evidence-Driven Sensing Schedules for ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2611.00439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) lets a base station detect human motion with the same signals it uses for data, but every sensing transmission takes resources from users. Sensing rarely while nothing moves saves resources, yet a brief hand gesture by an otherwise still person can then start and end between two transmissions and go unnoticed. We propose an evidence-driven schedule, based on data-efficient cumulative-sum (CuSum) change detection, that pauses sensing while measurements indicate no motion and senses continuously once they suggest motion. It is adapted to orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) sensing, where requests can be blocked by data traffic and measurements arrive late, and evaluated with an articulated human model of limb motion. In simulations without wall reflections, with the same monitoring budget and below one false alarm per minute, it detects 1.5--4.2 times as many limb movements within 200~ms as periodic sensing. A tuned two-rate trigger performs similarly, and the gain over periodic sensing persists, without retuning or cost matching, in a simulated room with wall reflections. Under a small budget, measurements should decide when to sense.
item.dc:creator: Seyed Bagher Hashemi Natanzi, Bo Tang

item.title: FESTiVE: Self-calibrated Spatial-temporal Gradient Characterization for Non-cartesian Imaging on High Performance Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gradient imperfections disrupt the encoding benefits of long-readout imaging applications on high-performance systems. Currently, external field monitoring hardware provides the only reliable solution for general spatial-temporal gradient characterization. We present FESTiVE, a data-driven alternative to higher-order field monitoring. FESTiVE leverages parallel imaging to both implicitly model and explicitly recover field imperfections. Using a fast k-t mapping calibration scan, FESTiVE formulates a time-varying GRAPPA problem which maps k-space data corrupted by a time-varying gradient imperfection against a clean reference. This mapping is represented compactly with an implicit neural representation, from which the spatial-temporal fields are recovered in image space using coil sensitivities. In phantom, FESTiVE produces comparable field measurements to a Skope field camera across multiple non-cartesian 2D acquisition strategies and gradient specifications. In vivo, FESTiVE achieves state-of-the-art image quality for a high-performance diffusion spiral protocol on the head-only MAGNUS 3T, where higher-order phase imperfections are significant. At 7T, on the head-only Siemens TerraX system, FESTiVE enables 300{\mu}m spiral imaging where conventional field camera-based approaches fall below probe dephasing limits. In conclusion, FESTiVE enables robust high-resolution non-cartesian imaging on high-performance gradients, characterizing gradient imperfections using parallel imaging rather than field monitoring hardware.

item.title: RayAR: Autoregressive Dominant Path Generation for Low-Overhead MIMO Beam Alignment
item.description: arXiv:2611.00560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beam alignment in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems requires selecting suitable transmit and receive beam pairs with limited measurement overhead. Although 3GPP Release 18 investigates beam prediction from partial measurements, collecting these measurements still incurs probing overhead. Geometry can focus this probing through the departure and arrival directions of dominant paths, whose identification requires accounting for coupled diffraction interactions. To address this challenge, we propose RayAR, an autoregressive method that generates dominant propagation paths from urban geometry. RayAR conditions candidate ranking on the path prefix, local diffraction geometry, and receiver reachability, updating this context after each selection until the receiver becomes visible. The completed path's departure and arrival directions rank beam pairs for probing, allowing the pair with the highest received power to be selected from a small candidate set. Under 3GPP Release 18 beam-management metrics, RayAR reduces probing by 96.88\% relative to exhaustive sweeping and achieves the highest optimal-pair hit rate among compared methods at the same budget. Real-world measurements further demonstrate the accuracy of this geometric guidance, with simulation-trained RayAR achieving the lowest departure and arrival angular errors among compared methods without fine-tuning and a mean arrival-direction error of 9.07$^\circ$.
item.dc:creator: Junxi Huang, Xiucheng Wang, Nan Cheng, Kailong Wang, Jiang Guo, Yuxiang Zhang

item.title: Synergy-Aware Symbol Allocation for Distributed Semantic Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.00648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed semantic communication enables spatially separated terminals to support collaborative inference over wireless links for 6G edge intelligence. In multimodal sensing and cooperative perception, a single terminal captures only a partial view, and full task semantics emerge only when complementary observations from multiple terminals are fused at the receiver. However, under tight uplink budgets, existing task-oriented joint source--channel coding (JSCC) and distributed information bottleneck (IB) methods evaluate rate--distortion trade-offs per terminal, tending to undervalue cross-terminal synergistic features and prune them prematurely. To address this issue, we propose a synergy-credited distributed JSCC (\method{}) framework that introduces a differentiable, post-equalization matrix R\'enyi synergy credit as a surrogate to reward complementary task evidence surviving the wireless channel and backpropagates its gradients to local symbol gates. At deployment, the credit branch is removed and binary symbol masks are frozen, allowing each terminal to encode independently without inter-terminal signaling or extra inference overhead. Experiments show that \method{} recovers the analytical symbol-selection threshold on parity sources and reduces payload symbols by 28.4\% on AV-MNIST and 32.9\% on PAMAP2 over an uncredited gated baseline, while achieving a 6.2-point accuracy gain at $-6$~dB under 3GPP TDL-C fading with pilot-aided channel estimation for low-overhead wireless cooperative sensing.
item.dc:creator: Fan Gao, Youzheng Wang, Zhijin Qin, Xiaoming Tao

item.title: Robust 3DMA GNSS Positioning in Urban Areas Using Conservative Candidate Set Determination Based on GNSS Shadow and Reflection
item.description: arXiv:2611.00696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In urban environments, global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning is often degraded by signal blockage and reflection caused by surrounding buildings. To address this problem, various three-dimensional mapping-aided (3DMA) GNSS techniques have been proposed. Among them, zonotope shadow and reflection matching (ZSRM) has demonstrated effective positioning performance by determining the candidate receiver position set using predicted GNSS shadow and reflection regions. However, ZSRM remains vulnerable to satellite signal misclassification, which may lead to positioning failure. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a conservative candidate set determination strategy for robust ZSRM positioning. Instead of using only the most probable signal reception condition from an artificial intelligence (AI)-based classifier, the proposed method combines the candidate regions associated with the two most probable classes. This allows the candidate receiver position set to be determined more conservatively, reducing the risk of positioning failure under signal misclassification. The proposed method was evaluated using real-world urban GNSS data. Experimental results show that the proposed method improved the positioning success rate to 100% for RF, GBDT, and SVM classifiers, compared with 8.2%-30.1% for the existing ZSRM algorithm using individual classifier outputs and 96.6% for ZSRM with unanimous voting. Although the proposed method increased the position bounds by retaining additional candidate regions, it produced smaller position bounds than ZSRM with unanimous voting. These results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially enhances the robustness of ZSRM under satellite signal misclassification in urban GNSS environments.
item.dc:creator: Sanghyun Kim, Jiwon Seo

item.title: Embodied AI for Radio Mapping: From Solo to Swarm
item.description: arXiv:2611.00770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio maps provide spatial knowledge of wireless environments to assess coverage, manage spectrum use, and support connectivity-aware mobility. Recent advances in embodied intelligence (EI) offer a promising approach to radio map reconstruction by enabling agents to perceive the environment and autonomously adjust their survey paths toward safe, reachable locations. However, a single agent remains constrained by limited endurance and onboard computing capacity, limiting measurement collection and reconstruction performance. Swarm cooperation can support more efficient radio mapping over larger areas by sharing observations and coordinating members' sampling. This article first explores the capabilities and applications of cooperative embodied agents. A cooperative radio map reconstruction framework is then presented, together with its key enabling techniques. Case study results illustrate how scene perception supports access to informative sampling locations and how air--ground cooperation improves reconstruction through complementary measurements and mobile support. The article concludes with open challenges and future research directions for reliable and efficient embodied cooperative radio mapping in complex environments.
item.dc:creator: Shangjie Zhuang, Wenlihan Lu, Zhentian Zhang, Ziwei Huang, Zaichen Zhang, Rongqing Zhang, Shijian Gao

item.title: Joint Transmit Power and Reflection Coefficient Optimization for Underlay Cognitive Radio Ambient Backscatter Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.00801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of cognitive radio (CR) technology with backscatter communication offers a promising solution for developing spectrum-efficient and low-power wireless networks. In this paper, we investigate the performance of an underlay cognitive radio ambient backscatter communication (CR-AmBC) system operating under primary network (PN) interference constraints. The objective is to maximize the performance of the CR-AmBC system while protecting the PN from interference. Differing from prior work, our formulation jointly accounts for: (i) interference from the PN on the CR receivers, (ii) interference from the backscatter device (BD) on the PN receiver, and (iii) imperfect successive interference cancellation (i-SIC) at the secondary destination. We propose a joint transmit power and reflection coefficient optimization framework that incorporates the minimum data rate requirements, the PN interference constraint, and i-SIC for decoding the BD signal. The nonconvex problem is decomposed into two subproblems solved via alternating optimization: (a) a closed-form expression for the feasible transmit power given a fixed reflection coefficient, and (b) an efficient one-dimensional search for the reflection coefficient. We prove that the power update is optimal, reducing the joint problem to a one-dimensional search, with monotone convergence and $\mathcal{O}(KN_\beta)$ complexity for $K$ iterations and $N_\beta$ search points. We present a comprehensive simulation-based performance evaluation and the results demonstrate that the proposed joint transmission power and reflection coefficient optimization provides an effective strategy to maximize the performance of the CR-AmBC system without violating the PN protection constraints.
item.dc:creator: Chabalala S. Chabalala, Peter Odero Akuon, Zhen Gao

item.title: Service-Area Robust NOMA for Pinching Antennas Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) enable near-field beam focusing using radiating points along a dielectric waveguide, but coherent spherical-wave superposition makes their channels sensitive to small user displacements. This sensitivity is critical for power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), where successive interference cancellation (SIC) requires the weak-user layer to remain decodable at the strong user. We develop spatially robust PASS-NOMA designs that optimize antenna placement and power splitting over bounded service areas (SAs), with a preset decoding order and explicit SIC-feasibility constraints. We propose a worst-case design for quasi-static users and an ergodic design for codewords spanning representative SA positions, and characterize their achievable rate regions. Numerical results show that, despite SIC requiring weak-user decoding in both SAs, NOMA outperforms orthogonal multiple access (OMA) with a shared placement under both robustness models except when the strong user is served at low rate. In the ergodic regime, this advantage can persist even against OMA with per-user antenna reconfiguration.

item.title: Low-PAPR Rank-2 DFT-s-OFDM Waveform for 6G Uplink
item.description: arXiv:2611.00862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rank-2 discrete Fourier transform-spread orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DFT-s-OFDM) is attracting renewed interest for 6G uplink, offering not only spatial multiplexing gains but also an additional degree of freedom for peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction. We exploit this freedom by selectively exchanging constellation symbols between the two layers before DFT spreading, preserving the transmitted information while reshaping the resulting waveforms. Building on this idea, we propose Cyclic Layer Assignment with Shared-basis Synthesis (CLASS). CLASS employs carefully designed cyclic assignment patterns to generate diverse waveform candidates, while reusing a small number of waveform components to avoid synthesizing each candidate separately. We further establish the optimality of the cyclic design in maximizing waveform diversity under a minimum-basis constraint when equal group sizes are feasible. With only six inverse DFTs, CLASS explores 16 assignments and reduces the 99th-percentile worst-layer PAPR by 1.41 dB relative to fixed assignment, outperforming representative selected mapping (SLM) and partial transmit sequences (PTS) schemes under the same synthesis budget.
item.dc:creator: Yewen Cao, Fen Hou, Yulin Shao

item.title: Harnessing Inter-Waveguide Evanescent Coupling in Pinching-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In multi-waveguide pinching-antenna systems (PASS), waveguides are typically modeled as independent signal-transport paths. However, when dielectric waveguides are closely spaced, their evanescent electromagnetic fields overlap, allowing guided signals to exchange energy before radiation. While such inter-waveguide coupling is conventionally regarded as undesirable crosstalk, this paper reveals an opportunity to harness it as an additional analog beamforming resource. The key insight is that coupling, through its interaction with sequential signal extraction by distributed pinching antennas (PAs), can reshape coherent signal combining at the receivers without increasing the available signal power. Consequently, stronger coupling does not necessarily yield better performance; rather, the coupling-induced phase relationships determine whether the radiated signals combine constructively or destructively. To characterize and exploit this mechanism, we establish a physics-based end-to-end channel model, derive coupling-aware waveguide-spacing principles and achievable-rate bounds, and develop joint waveguide deployment, PA placement, and digital precoding algorithms for multi-hotspot communications. Numerical results demonstrate substantial sum-rate improvements over conventional fixed-deployment and optimized minimum-spacing PASS benchmarks. These findings establish inter-waveguide evanescent coupling as a new physical degree of freedom for PASS channel reconfiguration.
item.dc:creator: Dengke Wei, Runxin Zhang, Yulin Shao, Shaodan Ma

item.title: Multi-Antenna Channel Prediction in 5G and Beyond using Data driven approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.00869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Wireless Communication evolves towards 5G and beyond, it satisfies Quality of Service (QoS) requirements of users by utilizing beam forming, adaptive transmission and multi antenna communication techniques. It is essential to have accurate channel information at Base station (BS) to provide satisfactory QoS to users. Traditional channel estimation approach involves transmitting pilots from User Equipments (UEs) and estimating the channel at BS, increases computational complexity as it is periodic process. It also increases communication complexity as number of antennas at BS increases which leads to increase in pilots. In this paper, we consider channel vector prediction using Machine learning approach at 7GHz. In this work, we generated data using ray tracing mechanism and used this generated data to train Machine learning models. We Considered XG Boost regression and Multilayer perceptron regression model.
item.dc:creator: A. Sathi Babu, V. Udaya Sankar, Vishnu Ram OV

item.title: Denoising Multiuser Interference Enabled Iterative AI Receiver
item.description: arXiv:2611.00910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When interfering users transmit finite-alphabet symbols, the aggregate of multiuser interference and thermal noise in a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) receiver is generally non-Gaussian. Its covariance alone does not specify the likelihood required for Bayesian detection. Conventional minimum mean-square error interference rejection combining (MMSE-IRC) is optimal among linear estimators with known second-order statistics, but it does not generally attain the Bayesian MMSE estimate in this setting. In this article, we propose an iterative artificial intelligence (AI) receiver that jointly refines interference cancellation, channel estimation, and desired-user detection. At each iteration, an interference denoising network reconstructs the received interference from the residual observation, covariance information, and uncertainty in the desired-user soft decisions. After cancellation, the preceding soft decisions support successive interference cancellation among desired-user streams and yield least squares (LS) channel estimates at data positions. A channel estimation network refines these estimates using the preceding channel estimate. Finally, MMSE-IRC preprocessing provides an effective channel matrix and soft symbol estimates to a Transformer-ResNet-PIC detector, which produces symbol probabilities for the next iteration. We also relate these structured detector inputs to the likelihood gradient of a relaxed Bayesian detection problem. The resulting receiver uses soft decisions to couple the three processing stages across iterations. Link-level simulations show that denoising multiuser interference enables the proposed iterative AI receiver to approach the attainable theoretical performance bound. The proposed receiver substantially outperforms the conventional quasi-ML receiver based on LMMSE channel estimation and MMSE-IRC preprocessing.
item.dc:creator: Xiangzhao Qin, Sha Hu, Jing Qian, Hao Wang

item.title: Channel Estimation for Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces with Mutual Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Channel estimation for stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) has relied on the cascade model, which ignores mutual coupling and inter-layer reflection. Under a coupling-consistent multiport model, we show that the pilots are linear in the unknown channel segments and derive least-squares and linear minimum-mean-square-error estimators, an identifiability condition and an exact error decomposition for the reactance training schedule, and a gradient-based schedule design. Cascade-based estimation floors above $0$~dB normalized error at practical layer spacings and collapses the sum rate below that of the bare feed, whereas the proposed estimators retain about $80\%$ of the perfect-channel-knowledge sum rate.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Kumar Sheemar, Giovanni Iacovelli, Symeon Chatzinotas

item.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting: A New Paradigm for Wireless Environment Representation
item.description: arXiv:2611.01122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless channels are shaped by the surrounding propagation environment, making explicit environment representation an effective approach for characterizing channels. By combining explicit environment modeling with learnable radio frequency characteristics, 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) emerges as a new paradigm for wireless environment representation. This article establishes a systematic perspective on 3DGS-enabled wireless communications in terms of environment representation. We first clarify the rationale for extending 3DGS from visual scene modeling to wireless communications and formulate a unified framework for wireless environment representation. Building on this framework, we further investigate the applicability of 3DGS-based representations to a broad range of communication and sensing tasks, and characterize key considerations for practical deployment. Finally, emerging directions are highlighted, including cross-scene generalization, near-field channel modeling, real-world data collection, and lifecycle management.
item.dc:creator: Jinya Zhang, Jiajia Guo, Chao-Kai Wen, Shi Jin

item.title: Fundamental Limits and Joint Design for Monostatic Joint Communications and Sensing in LEO Satellites
item.description: arXiv:2611.01164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monostatic joint communication and sensing (JCAS) from a low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite requires full-duplex (FD) operation, with self-interference (SI) $80$--$100$~dB stronger than the ground echo. The echo returns milliseconds after transmission, whereas the onboard coupling spans a few symbols. We develop a theory and a design that exploit this separation. Restricting the analog and digital cancellers to the short SI support is without loss of optimality and essential in practice: a least-squares canceller whose support contains the target delay absorbs the coherent echo and reduces the radar SINR by a closed-form factor, about $18$~dB for a vessel at its zero-Doppler crossing. Modeling the SI that no linear canceller can reconstruct as spatially white and accounting for ADC quantization, we derive in closed form a ceiling on the radar SINR, the minimum pre-ADC SI power under a canceller tap budget, the budget for full cancellation, and the sensing weight at which the optimal design changes over from communication to sensing. We then maximize a weighted sum of the communication and sensing SINRs, each normalized by its half-duplex benchmark, over the beamformers, sensing covariance, combiners, and cancellers for $K$ users and $Q$ targets, using an alternating algorithm with closed-form updates. Simulations confirm the closed forms. The joint design gains up to $13\%$ in the normalized objective over a sequential design that cancels the SI only at the receiver, and more than $10$~dB of downlink and radar SINR with $4$-bit ADCs and in the 10th-percentile worst-target SINR of four targets, whereas ignoring the SI overloads the ADCs.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Kumar Sheemar, Giovanni Iacovelli, Jorge Querol, Symeon Chatzinotas

item.title: SINR-Aware Adaptive Offloading and Resource Allocation in Shared-Spectrum Integrated Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.01169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sharing the sub-6~GHz spectrum between terrestrial networks and low Earth orbit satellites introduces cross-tier interference in both directions, as terrestrial transmissions can degrade satellite-link reception, while satellite transmissions can impair the performance of terrestrial links. Conventional reference signal received power (RSRP)-based offloading, designed for separate frequency bands, does not account for this cross-tier interference. We study offloading and resource allocation in an integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial network through a two-timescale framework in which signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR)-aware adaptive traffic offloading (SAATO) updates user associations from filtered SINR and load-aware expected throughput, switching a user only across a hysteresis band, while joint cross-tier fractional programming (Joint-FP) optimizes resource allocation for the resulting associations. Under an equal-share resource allocation model, the resulting decision metric approximates the change in proportional-fair utility with an error that decays with load. We prove that joint allocation under the sum-rate utility is nondeterministic polynomial-time (NP)-hard and that the utility sequence accepted by Joint-FP is non-decreasing and convergent. At full spectral overlap, RSRP-based offloading leaves 44\% of user samples below 0.5~Mbps (outage), whereas SAATO with Joint-FP, given instantaneous channel knowledge, leaves none and increases geometric-mean throughput by 8\% and 2\% under half and full spectral overlap, respectively, relative to power control without offloading. It also limits tier switching to at most 0.05 switches per user per minute.
item.dc:creator: Aman Khalid, Muhammad Sohaib Aslam, Ahmed Naeem, Seyit Karatepe, Muhammet Kirik, Huseyin Arslan

item.title: Device Identification and Motion Classification of Passive Nonlinear RF Transponders Using Wi-Fi Channel State Information
item.description: arXiv:2611.01254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A method of joint device authentication and gesture classification using low-cost passive transponders and 802.11 signals of opportunity from commodity hardware is presented for tracking objects in cluttered environments. The approach detects nonlinear responses of diode-based radio-frequency (RF) transponders by estimating the mean time-varying phase across all subcarrier channel state information (CSI) obtained from standard preambles. These unique responses are enabled by passive transponders utilizing 2.4 GHz meander-line monopole antennas with capacitive top-hat loading and a low-barrier Schottky diode, allowing for low-power omnidirectional sensing and complex gesture recognition across multiple unique devices. The capture system uses a wireless access point to illuminate the transponder with a standard preamble. This signal is modulated by the diode's nonlinear response and transmitted to a single ESP32 receiver to calculate the channel response. Using the modulated CSI, device identification via RF fingerprinting achieves >95% accuracy in both static and dynamic conditions using simple machine learning models. For dynamically moving transponders, a time-varying velocity profile is calculated using a novel phase sanitation approach that significantly reduces the impacts of the non-cooperative network. This enables high-accuracy estimation of micro-motions on a single receiver, achieving a theoretical limit of 9.75 m/s using an amplitude-invariant binary comparator form of the sanitized waveform. The concept is experimentally validated using lightweight CNN-LSTM deep-learning models applied to a diverse dataset of five transponders and three motion profiles. This experimental validation demonstrated a classification accuracy of 98% in both gesture classification and device identification tasks.
item.dc:creator: Cory Hilton, Jeffrey A. Nanzer

item.title: Trajectory Design and User Scheduling for Pinching-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite antenna movement speed introduces repositioning delays that can limit the performance gains of pinching-antenna systems. In this paper, a trajectory based scheme is proposed for a time division multiple access (TDMA) based pinching-antenna system, allowing transmission during both movement and stationary operation. A discrete-time model is developed to characterize periodic antenna trajectories and antenna-user service association under practical movement constraints. For a single-waveguide scenario, the expected average achievable rate is derived. The rate loss relative to instantaneous positioning and the rate improvement over a fixed antenna are further analyzed, with an upper bound on the former and a lower bound on the latter established. To improve fairness among users, a minimum average rate maximization problem is formulated through joint trajectory design and user scheduling. To address the coupling between these variables, an alternating optimization (AO) framework is adopted. Specifically, a successive convex approximation (SCA) based algorithm is developed using concave rate lower bounds, while a game based scheduling algorithm employs an ordered user-rate vector as the common utility. The convergence of the SCA objective value and the finite termination and stability of the scheduling algorithm are established. Simulation results demonstrate the gains achieved by the joint design and show that the proposed system can approach instantaneous-positioning performance under finite antenna movement speed.
item.dc:creator: Kaidi Wang, Daniel K. C. So, Zhiguo Ding

item.title: Distributed Pinching-Antenna Architecture for Communication and Target Positioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.01382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a pinching-antenna system (PASS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework for joint downlink communication and target positioning. The dielectric waveguides enable flexible signal radiation through activated pinching antennas (PAs), while the reflected echo signals are collected by a sensing receiver. A unified waveform is adopted to support both data transmission and sensing-echo processing. In particular, a two-stage procedure is developed for target localization using time-sum-of-arrival (TSoA) measurements, where the signal propagation distances are first estimated through de-chirp processing and beat frequency extraction. Then, the target position is obtained based on TSoA measurements using the weighted linear least squares(WLLS) technique. To characterize the fundamental limits of the PASS-assisted ISAC system, a Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRB) is derived, which captures the impact of PA activation. Furthermore, the PA activation problem is formulated to jointly optimize the communication spectral efficiency (SE) and sensing performance. To address this, a low-complexity heuristic greedy selection algorithm is proposed to determine the activated PA pattern. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms random PA selection, achieving gains of up to 81% improvement in communication SE.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Ni, Jiajun He, Mohammadali Mohammadi, Hien Quoc Ngo, Michail Matthaiou

item.title: Leveraging high-performance head-only gradients to enable ~2-fold higher multiband acceleration in SMS-EPI and SMS-EPTI
item.description: arXiv:2611.01405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-performance head-only gradient systems can substantially reduce echo spacing (ESP) in echo-planar imaging (EPI), but the resulting encoding speed is typically used to shorten readouts and reduce distortion. Here, we instead leverage the increased echo budget to enable denser k-space sampling and higher simultaneous-multislice (SMS) acceleration in SMS-EPI and SMS-EPTI. Fast k-space traversal with denser ky-kz sampling is achieved using peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS)-optimized gradient waveforms, while high-quality reconstruction is obtained using field-correcting GRAPPA (FCG). The resulting ESPs on MAGNUS 3T and Impulse 7T are approximately half those of high-performance whole-body systems, enabling approximately 2-fold higher multiband (MB) acceleration. This facilitates high-quality 2.5-mm isotropic whole-brain resting-state fMRI at 7T with MB28 and a repetition time (TR) of 123 ms.
item.dc:creator: Yimeng Lin, Zachary Shah, Mehdi Khalighi, Zimu Huo, Mengze Gao, Hua Wu, Baolian Yang, Qiang Liu, Erpeng Dai, Arthur Chakwizira, Lipeng Ning, Carl-Fredrik Westin, Yogesh Rathi, Jonathan R. Polimeni, Nan Wang, Adam B. Kerr, Kawin Setsompop

item.title: Label-Free Performance Estimation of Deep Learning Based Radar Detectors in Time-Varying Environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.01407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep-learning-based radar target detectors can achieve strong performance in complex sensing environments. However, in time-varying environments, changes in clutter characteristics may cause the distribution of echoes to deviate from that of the training data, thereby degrading detector reliability. Timely identification of such degradation requires an accurate assessment of the deployed detector's performance; however, ground-truth labels for radar echoes are typically unavailable during deployment. This paper investigates label-free performance estimation for deployed deep learning-based radar target detectors. We first show that confidence-based estimators tend to overestimate detection performance under distribution shift because they fail to account for the discrepancy between the detector-induced pseudo-label distribution and the true label distribution. To address this limitation, we propose probabilistic optimal transport (POT), which assesses deployment performance by computing the Wasserstein distance between the detector's output probability distribution on unlabeled deployment echoes and the label distribution in the training data. We further develop thresholded probabilistic optimal transport (TPOT), which suppresses the influence of anomalous transport costs on the Wasserstein-distance-based estimate, thereby improving estimation robustness. Experiments on a publicly measured radar dataset demonstrate that POT and TPOT consistently outperform representative label-free baselines across deployment scenarios with varying degrees of data distribution shift.
item.dc:creator: Chuanfei Zang, Yiru Lin, Yumiao Wang, Xingyu Chen, Xiaobo Yang, Guolong Cui

item.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Multi-User OFDM ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is envisioned as a key enabling technology for 6G networks. Efficient resource sharing between communication and sensing is a fundamental challenge in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ISAC systems, particularly in multi-user scenarios, where channel diversity can be exploited to improve resource utilization. This paper investigates joint subcarrier assignment and power allocation for a downlink multi-user OFDM ISAC system, with the objective of minimizing the delay Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRLB) subject to constraints on the normalized integrated sidelobe level (ISL) over the region of interest (RoI), per-user data rates, and total transmit power. We first derive a convex formulation for sensing power allocation given fixed subcarrier assignments, and then develop an equivalent mixed-integer conic formulation of the joint optimization problem. To obtain computationally tractable solutions, we propose a conic relaxation-guided fix-and-optimize (CRG-FO) algorithm that integrates continuous relaxation, power re-optimization under fixed subcarrier assignments, and restricted neighborhood search. Simulation results demonstrate that joint subcarrier and power allocation reduces the distance CRLB relative to uniform subcarrier and power allocation across the tested ISL thresholds, rate loads, and user configurations. Power optimization on uniform sensing supports captures most of this gain, while adaptive subcarrier assignment provides only modest additional improvement.
item.dc:creator: Jiayue Huang, Ning Wei, Min Qiu, Aimin Tang

item.title: Low-Latency Joint Source-Channel Coding with Multiple Constant Curvature Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.01476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose constant-curvature curve multicode (C3M), a multi-branch extension of constant-curvature curve tube (C3T) analog joint source-channel coding for one-shot transmission over fixed isotropic AWGN channels. Instead of mapping a scalar source to a single curve on the power sphere, C3M partitions the source interval across a union of constant-speed branch curves in even-dimensional Euclidean space. This construction increases the available geometric degrees of freedom while preserving a low block length analog encoding structure. We derive the induced mixture output distribution, posterior representation, MAP and MMSE estimators, and mutual-information decomposition into branch-identification and along-curve components. We then introduce geometry- and classification-aware branch allocation rules based on tube density, curve length, and branch-classification reliability. The resulting design procedure fixes the optimal C3T curve as a starting branch and sequentially selects additional branches, thereby reducing the combinatorial cost of exhaustive multi-curve search. We use NORM-inspired branch-conditioned spectral decoders based on Fourier-feature lifting of the received ambient vector. Numerical experiments in four and six dimensions show that adding candidate branch curves improves the finite-dimensional end-to-end signal-to-distortion ratio, with selected two- and three-candidate C3M systems outperforming the one-curve baseline at +10 dB SNR. The results show that multi-curve analog mappings provide a practical finite-dimensional design route for low block length joint source-channel coding.
item.dc:creator: Anders M. Buvarp, Stefan Werner

item.title: Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer for Joint Multipath Parameter Estimation: Applications to mmWave Positioning and Radio SLAM
item.description: arXiv:2611.01491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Future 6G wireless networks are expected to evolve toward AI-native systems that support intelligent, environment-aware services, including positioning and mapping. Current research has already integrated AI into several aspects of communication, particularly wireless channel estimation. However, most learning-based channel estimators focus on communication-oriented objectives rather than explicitly estimating multipath parameters such as delay, angle of arrival (AoA), and angle of departure (AoD). These parameters provide essential geometric information for downstream tasks including positioning and radio simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). In this work, we propose a Spectral-Convolutional Factorized Transformer (SCFT) for joint multipath component (MPC) estimation from noisy complex channel estimates and physical beam-pair descriptors. SCFT combines local spectral convolution, permutation-equivariant beam-set attention, and a query-based Transformer decoder to detect and classify line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) paths and estimate their observed delays, AoAs, and AoDs. Experiments on realistic ray-tracing data show that SCFT reduces the generalized optimal sub-pattern assignment (GOSPA) error by 13.4% compared with ResNet, the strongest competing baseline. We further demonstrate this advantage in independent snapshot positioning and radio SLAM, where SCFT reduces position RMSE by 18.5% and 65.0%, respectively, relative to ResNet. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly recovering multipath geometry, as improvements in MPC estimation can translate into substantial gains in downstream tasks.
item.dc:creator: Yaya Etiabi, Wessam Ajib, Halima Elbiaze

item.title: AI-Aided and AI-Oriented Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation: A Survey
item.description: arXiv:2611.01521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The evolution from 5G to 6G networks marks a transition toward the "intelligence of everything." While 5G enables enhanced connectivity, 6G aspires to embed intelligence directly into communication infrastructures, creating systems that are adaptive, context aware, and capable of autonomous decision making. Realizing such systems depends on harmonizing three fundamental functions that compete for shared network resources and often pursue conflicting goals: (i) sensing for environmental and contextual information acquisition, (ii) communication for reliable and timely information exchange, and (iii) computation for information processing and decision making. This harmonization necessitates shifting from independent optimization to their joint design as a unified system, a paradigm known as Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation (ISCC). In parallel, AI has emerged both as an enabling tool for ISCC optimization and as a workload whose requirements influence ISCC system design. This survey comprehensively examines ISCC from this dual perspective by distinguishing between AI-aided ISCC, in which learning-based methods support the joint design and optimization of sensing, communication, and computation, and AI-oriented ISCC, in which these functions are jointly configured to support learning, inference, and distributed intelligence. The survey further examines the co-design of AI and ISCC, where AI requirements and ISCC constraints jointly shape system and model decisions. It further provides a comparative synthesis of the resulting design approaches, system architectures, performance metrics, and evaluation practices, relates these developments to application-specific requirements across different domains, and identifies open research problems toward scalable, adaptive, and trustworthy AI-ISCC systems.
item.dc:creator: Yaya Etiabi, Wessam Ajib, El Mehdi Amhoud, Halima Elbiaze

item.title: Assessing Temporal Dispersion of Time-Varying Channel at 38 GHz for Different Reference Signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.01685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the influence of reference waveform selection on temporal dispersion estimation in a time-varying radio channel at 38 GHz. Three reference waveforms-numerically generated in MATLAB, measured through a conducted connection, and recorded in an anechoic chamber -are compared using the same wideband channel measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment. Their effects on the estimated power delay profiles (PDPs), mean delay, and root mean square (RMS) delay spread are evaluated. Despite noticeable differences in the time-domain and spectral characteristics of the reference waveforms, the resulting PDPs exhibit similar multipath structures, while the estimated temporal dispersion parameters show relatively small differences. The results indicate limited sensitivity to reference waveform selection under the investigated measurement conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Wojtu\'n, Bartosz Czaja, Tomasz Grasza, Rafa{\l} Przesmycki, Jan M. Kelner, Cezary Zi\'o{\l}kowski, Radek Zavorka, Josef Vychodil, Tomas Mikulasek, Jiri Blumenstein, Ales Prokes, Aniruddha Chandra

item.title: Domain-Aware Hierarchical Federated Learning for UAV Swarms Across Heterogeneous Environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.01812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hierarchical federated learning (HFL) enables communication-efficient training in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms, but performance degrades under changing and heterogeneous environments. This paper proposes domain-aware HFL (DA-HFL), integrating mobility-informed clustering, cluster-level aggregation, cloud-based Fisher-weighted merging, a domain-adversarial shared backbone, environment-specific heads, and gated inference with local adaptation. A mission-weighted optimization formulation incorporates energy, latency, and cluster-head eligibility constraints. Theoretical analysis establishes resource feasibility, a conditional backbone-stationarity bound, the quadratic optimality of Fisher-weighted merging, and communication and computation complexity bounds. Simulations across four heterogeneous environments demonstrate faster convergence, improved accuracy during environmental transitions, and more stable, purer clusters than the evaluated baselines, with modest energy overhead over resource-aware HFL. Ablation studies validate the contributions of the proposed components.
item.dc:creator: Taha Mahmood, Mudassar Shakeel, Ahmed Naeem, El Mehdi Amhoud, Rizwan Ahmad, Salman Ghafoor

item.title: FADE: A Flow-Based Approach for Multichannel Tail Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.01849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) is vulnerable to rare low-received-power events, and the spatial-diversity benefits of multiple receivers can be significantly reduced when they experience simultaneous deep fading. Multivariate Extreme Value Theory (MEVT) provides a principled framework for characterizing such joint tail behavior. However, conventional MEVT methods often rely on restrictive parametric assumptions or discrete representations of the dependence structure, which may not fully capture complex multivariate tail behavior. This paper proposes Flow-based Angular Density Estimation (FADE), a flow-based approach for characterizing the dependence between extreme events across receivers within the MEVT framework. FADE transforms multivariate extremes into a standard extreme-value representation and uses a flow-based density estimator to learn the dependence structure from the transformed data without imposing a predefined parametric form. The proposed framework is evaluated using experimentally collected data from a UAV communication system, in which the UAV serves as the transmitter and communicates with two ground receivers. FADE provides closer agreement with the empirical joint CDF, achieving reductions of up to 22.4% in MAE compared with the state-of-the-art Logistic and Maximum Empirical Likelihood (MEL) methods, while also improving distributional agreement and reducing absolute bias.
item.dc:creator: Parmida Valiahdi, Niloofar Mehrnia, Mustafa Furkan Beker, Ubeydullah Erdemir, Ibrahim Hokelek, Sinem Coleri

item.title: Ray-Tracing-Parameter-Based Lightweight Hybrid Precoding via Cascade XGBoost for Wideband Massive MIMO-OFDM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid precoding reduces the radio-frequency (RF) hardware burden in wideband massive MIMO-OFDM systems, but conventional optimization and deep neural network (DNN)-based approaches can incur high online complexity. This paper proposes XGB-SVD, a lightweight hybrid precoding framework that maps compact ray-tracing path parameters directly to analog beamforming codeword indices using cascade eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). The cascade captures sequential beam-selection dependencies and transmit--receive propagation correlation, while the digital precoder and combiner are obtained from the reduced-dimensional equivalent channel using singular value decomposition (SVD). Evaluations over five DeepMIMO scenarios spanning sub-6-GHz and millimeter-wave bands show that XGB-SVD consistently outperforms the considered DNN baselines and approaches simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) in several environments. Cross-scenario results further indicate improved transfer from propagation-diverse training environments, while XGB-SVD provides lower online computational and training costs than the DNN baselines.
item.dc:creator: Po-Heng Chou, Wei-Chen Lin, Wan-Jen Huang, Walid Saad, Ronald Y. Chang

item.title: Green Learning-Based Signal-Level Detection of RIS Spoofing Attacks in Vehicular ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless infrastructure to jointly support communication and environmental sensing, but also introduces new physical-layer security threats. A malicious reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) can manipulate its time-varying reflection phases to generate spoofing echoes and distort the sensing results of a roadside unit (RSU). Existing trajectory-level detectors rely on reconstructed sensing parameters and vehicle trajectories, making their performance dependent on upstream estimation accuracy. In this paper, we propose a signal-level Green Learning (GL) framework that directly detects RIS spoofing from matched-filtered RSU echoes. The proposed method combines two-stage Subspace Approximation with Adjusted Bias (SAAB), Discriminant Feature Test (DFT), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for spatial-temporal representation learning, feature selection, and classification, respectively. Simulation results show 99.335\% detection accuracy for a 32-element malicious RIS at $-80$ dBm receiver noise power. GL remains competitive with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) baselines while requiring only 0.1119 million floating-point operations (FLOPs), and also generalizes to previously unseen RIS sizes.
item.dc:creator: Po-Heng Chou, Tingyu Shui, Pin-Qi Fu, Lien-Sheng Chang, Walid Saad, Li-Chun Wang

item.title: Clock Offsets and Ranges from Optical Pseudoranges
item.description: arXiv:2611.02214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note describes the estimation of ranges and clock offsets from measured pseudoranges in the context of the Kepler Navigation System. The latter system continuously adapts the frequency of its clocks to ensure that they all show the same time independently of where they are. In Medium Earth Orbits, the joint problem of estimating ranges and clock offsets can then be factorized.
item.dc:creator: Christoph G\"unther

item.title: Joint PAPR Reduction and Over-the-Air Computing in Multi-User OFDMA Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction challenge of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems utilizing tone reservation (TR) under an over-the-air computing constraint, such that the signals placed in the reserved tones simultaneously enable distributed computation at the receiver. To that end, the problem is cast as a fractional programming problem and solved via the iterative quadratic transform (QT), which guarantees convergence to a stationary point. A key contribution is the decomposition of the reserved-tone vector into an orthogonal pair of components: one satisfying the sum-computation constraint and the other providing the remaining degrees of freedom for PAPR reduction. This decomposition reveals that the proposed method and the benchmark sacrifices the same number of degrees of freedom. However, the proposed design distributes the computational payload across all reserved tones, yielding superior robustness against multi-user interference and quantization noise. Analytical and simulation results confirm that the proposed method matches the benchmark in PAPR reduction while outperforming it in computation accuracy, particularly in multi-user scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Getuar Rexhepi, Kuranage Roche Rayan Ranasinghe, Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu, David Gonz\'alez G

item.title: Joint Delay--Doppler Modeling of Multipath LEO Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.02350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multipath channel models for Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) non-terrestrial network (NTN) must contend with time variability due to rapid satellite orbital motion that in turn impacts local (near terrestrial) scattering near the ground terminal (GT) receiver. While 3GPP-defined NTN channel model pipelines TR 38.811, 38.901 incorporate elevation-dependence into statistical channel generators, these are inherited largely from 2-D terrestrial propagation and are largely insufficient. Further, they do not prescribe any integrated workflow that is broadly available for generating joint delay, Doppler/phase and component multipath power profiles as a function of satellite location over a pass. This work addresses this gap by developing a geometry-based stochastic channel model driven by prescribed slant range, elevation, and azimuth over a LEO pass. A ground scene generates wall-reflected, ground-reflected, and roof-edge-diffracted components, from which joint delay-Doppler statistics and temporal channel impulse response (CIR) evolution are obtained. The resulting locally wide-sense stationary tapped-delay-line CIR enables analysis of key statistics such as the $K$-factor of the taps, multipath delay and Doppler spreads as a function of elevation and scene parameters. Depending on the scenarios (urban and rural), our model-based results show that with omnidirectional antennas, the LoS probability, delay-spread and $K$-factor trends broadly match 3GPP NTN models in TR 38.811 as a function of elevation. Beamforming instead produces a mid-elevation $K$-factor peak, which is not predicted by TR 38.811 and 6G NTN. Doppler spreads are smaller than those from our previous model and QuaDriGa because the proposed model accounts for path existence. Stationarity durations for CIR are reported and generally decrease with elevation, but with local increases at mid-elevation due to path geometry effects.
item.dc:creator: Kuan-Po Chiu, Sumit Roy

item.title: Clock-Shift-Aided Blind Doppler Matching in Passive SDR Monitoring Data for LEO Doppler Positioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.02377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite signals have recently attracted increasing attention as opportunistic signals for positioning, navigation, and timing. Most Doppler-based LEO positioning studies rely on tracked satellite signals or raw in-phase/quadrature (IQ) samples that preserve signal-level structures for acquisition, Doppler tracking, or satellite association. In contrast, passive software-defined radio (SDR) monitoring systems often retain only time-frequency power scans, in which LEO Doppler traces appear as unlabeled ridges without raw IQ samples or identifiable signal structures. This paper proposes a clock-shift-aided segment-based blind Doppler matching method that associates unlabeled Doppler traces with candidate satellites predicted using two-line element (TLE) data. The proposed framework consists of slope-consistent Doppler segment generation, clock-shift-aided temporal alignment, and multi-metric satellite matching based on Doppler-rate and trajectory-shape consistency. The proposed method was evaluated using a three-hour subset of open Starlink/OneWeb monitoring data collected in the United Kingdom. The clock-offset search selected an effective offset of +19 s, for which 56 of 69 segments had at least one slope-compatible candidate, compared with 19 segments at zero shift. Using the resulting satellite associations, the batch positioning error over the full three-hour period was 104.2 m, whereas the RMSE-based and slope-based simple-segment baselines failed to converge near the reference receiver location.
item.dc:creator: Seunghyeon Park, Gaeun Kim, Jiwon Seo

item.title: A Beam-Switched Sparse Circular Array for Passive Wi-Fi Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.02378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wi-Fi sensing applications require unambiguous angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation over the full azimuth plane. Uniform circular arrays (UCAs) are shown to remove this ambiguity, but deploying the four RF chains typically available on commercial Wi-Fi chipsets into a sparse layout suffers from spatial undersampling. Such undersampling produces strong grating lobes. To overcome this hardware bottleneck, we first establish a generalized array manifold incorporating element radiation patterns, revealing the suitability and degradation mechanisms of directional UCAs. Then we propose an angularly staggered beam-switched UCA architecture that leverages the spatial complementarity. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed scheme effectively mitigates grating-lobe ambiguities without increasing the number of RF chains, significantly reducing AoA estimation outliers and improving omnidirectional tracking performance.
item.dc:creator: Yang Chen, Riccardo Bersan, Daniele Piazza, Stefano Savazzi, Michele D'Amico

item.title: Nearest Is Not Safest: Fluid-Antenna Port Selection for Over-the-Air Backpropagation in Urban Multipath
item.description: arXiv:2611.02384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over-the-air backpropagation returns a loss gradient through the reciprocal channel, which requires the return port to see the channel of the forward port. If the terminal moves in between, a fluid antenna system can return through the port nearest to the forward position. In ray-traced Chicago streets, with a pedestrian displacement of about half a wavelength and a street-level base station, this rule reverses 20 percent of the gradients at a port spacing of 0.7 wavelengths and 49 percent at 0.9 wavelengths, while one of the four nearest ports stays aligned in all but 2 and 9 percent. We derive a certificate for the sign of the mean correlation from the second moment of a planar angular spectrum. It reduces to a linear program with three variables and infinitely many constraints, is tight, and holds over a region of second moments. In a static Gaussian model, observations collected along a line cannot tell an angular spectrum from its mirror image, so the sign of the cross moment must come from other information. At unsurveyed positions of the same city, a knowledge map that transports surveyed paths through virtual sources and fits them to the causal channel history lowers the reversal rate at 0.9 wavelengths from 49 to 27 percent. Its gain over the nearest port survived every tested error, while its gain over a geometry rule stayed significant at the tested single-error levels of 5 degrees of phase drift per step and 2 mm of position error but not at the next tested levels. Without any survey, across five cities and ten base stations, the nearest port reverses 37 percent of the returns at 0.9 wavelengths and a rule based on the direction and elevation of the base station 20.5 percent. The multilayer perceptrons we tested did not beat these physical rules by the margin fixed in advance in the primary settings.
item.dc:creator: Xianzhong Li, Yuzhi Yang, Tianhao Guo

item.title: Which Chains to Calibrate for Physical Backpropagation: Per-User Factors Versus Base-Station Chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.02390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In physical backpropagation, users return loss derivatives over the time-division duplex uplink, giving the base station the downlink gradient without channel reconstruction. Reciprocity calibration conventionally prioritizes base-station chains, as column-normalized zero-forcing reduces a per-user factor to a stream rotation. This priority can reverse. With ideal base-station chains and no noise, per-user amplitude errors make the returned field a weighted sum-rate gradient. With zero-forcing full service at both optima, the loss is independent of array size. Otherwise the selection penalty, serving the wrong users, carries 86 to 94 percent of the amplitude-induced loss in five of six configurations. Per-user phase errors mainly slow the iteration. Base-station chain errors scale the returned field per antenna, and at 3 dB and 25 degrees they cost one user 1.3 dB of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) that no array size removes. With 80 users, such errors on both sides, and mismatched pilots, oracle per-user and base-station calibration leave 6.2 and 12.3 percent loss at 256 antennas on clustered channels. This ordering holds at 30 dB SNR and reverses for 1 dB, 10 degree user errors. A capped one-echo estimator comes within 2.4 percentage points of oracle per-user calibration but underperforms no calibration at 10 dB SNR.
item.dc:creator: Xianzhong Li, Yuzhi Yang, Tianhao Guo

item.title: MirrorComm: A Communication-Efficient Cooperative Perception Framework via Mirrored World Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.02405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperative perception (CP) requires substantial communication bandwidth to exchange sensing information among connected agents. A variety of compression techniques have been proposed to reduce transmission costs while retaining task-relevant information. However, most existing methods follow a frame-wise compression paradigm, overlooking temporal predictability and repeatedly transmitting information that could be inferred from historical context. To address these limitations, we propose MirrorComm, the first world model-based communication-efficient CP framework. Specifically, mirrored world models at the transmitter and receiver predict the transmitter's current observation from a shared history of its reconstructed observations. The transmitter compares this prediction with its current observation and selectively transmits observation updates to correct prediction errors, reducing repeated transmission of predictable information. Experiments on the OPV2V dataset across two downstream tasks including object detection and semantic segmentation show that MirrorComm reduces communication bandwidth requirements by up to approximately 66-fold while maintaining comparable performance to a state-of-the-art (SOTA) method. Ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the individual components.
item.dc:creator: Shenghan Luo, Yin Xu, Cixiao Zhang, Yang Wang, Yujie Cao, Zhuoran Xiao, Wenjun Zhang

item.title: Learned Diffusion Channel Priors for Coded MIMO Turbo Receivers
item.description: arXiv:2611.02486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterative receivers for coded multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) links estimate the channel from pilots, decoded data, and a prior. In short packets with few pilots and at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the prior matters. An expectation propagation (EP) turbo receiver needs the channel's mean and covariance given an anisotropic Gaussian message from the pilots and decoder. A diffusion prior's denoiser, however, returns only a mean, and only for a channel in isotropic noise. We replace only the receiver's channel-prior module with a learned diffusion prior. At an isotropic query formed from the message, one network gives both moments: its output is the mean, its Jacobian the covariance. They form a matrix-valued EP site, the Gaussian factor representing the prior. We show why an indefinite Jacobian can make the receiver diverge, and we floor its eigenvalues. In coded block error rate (BLER), the diffusion prior fails less than a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) prior learned from the same channels. It does so on a controlled sparse specular model and a 3GPP model, at every tested receive-array and training-set size. On the former, scalar-site controls, with one variance instead of the covariance, keep this advantage, so the gain comes from the diffusion prior.
item.dc:creator: Taejun Ha, Hyeji Kim, Jeonghun Park

item.title: Vehicle Speed-Aware Jammer-Resilient Receiver for Multi-User MIMO V2X Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication plays a crucial role in enabling connected and autonomous driving by supporting the reliable exchange of safety-critical information among vehicles and infrastructure. However, due to the open nature of wireless channels, V2X systems are vulnerable to various physical-layer attacks, among which jamming is one of the most intuitive and severe threats. In this paper, we propose a vehicle speed-aware jammer-resilient reception framework for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) V2X systems. The proposed method exploits the fundamental difference in Doppler characteristics between stationary jammers and moving vehicles. By transforming the received signal into the Doppler domain, the receiver identifies low-Doppler components associated with static interference and suppresses them through Doppler-domain filtering. Notably, the proposed approach does not require prior knowledge of the jammer channel or its spatial direction, making it suitable for practical V2X environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively mitigates strong jamming signals and significantly improves the achievable sum-rate compared with conventional receivers.
item.dc:creator: Hanyoung Park, Yongjae Jang, Ji-Woong Choi

item.title: First-Principles Channel Model and Capacity-Achieving Transmission Scheme in Thermal Noise Backscatter Links
item.description: arXiv:2611.02562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal noise communication systems transmit information by modulating thermal radiation, eliminating the need for a dedicated signal power source and making them attractive solutions for low-power sensor networks. Their efficiency enables long-lived, unobtrusive operation, which is valuable in the Internet of Things, electromagnetic interference-sensitive environments, and RFID tag systems. However, a limited understanding of the wireless channel model and efficient transmission schemes has hindered their practical deployment. Here, we present a wireless channel model that elucidates how systems operating at ambient temperature can modulate thermal noise to convey information. Our results reveal a thermal noise backscatter mechanism that enables significantly higher data rates than previously achieved. We designed and built a thermal noise communication system leveraging this mechanism to achieve data rates in the kilobits-per-second range - over two orders of magnitude higher than prior demonstrations. We also derive the system capacity and show that using polar codes, we are able to achieve this expected capacity. Our channel model and transmission scheme pave the way for new strategies in thermal noise sensing and communication, advancing practical low-power networking for next-generation wireless applications.
item.dc:creator: Geneva Ecola, Jida Zhang, Joseph M. Kahn, Zerina Kapetanovic

item.title: Energy-Efficient Tri-Hybrid Beamforming with Movable Pattern-Reconfigurable Antennas
item.description: arXiv:2611.02563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional hybrid precoding is confined to the digital/analog domains, leaving the spatial and radiation-pattern degrees-of-freedoms (DoFs) largely untapped. To unlock these, we propose a movable pattern-reconfigurable antenna (MPRA) and an energy-efficient tri-hybrid framework that jointly optimizes the precoders, antenna positions, and radiation-pattern states. We develop a hardware-inspired power model capturing the energy and transmission-time costs of antenna reconfiguration. The resulting mixed discrete-continuous fractional problem is solved via an alternating-optimization framework combining fractional programming, Riemannian optimization, and switching-aware pattern optimization. Simulations demonstrate near-exhaustive-search performance and consistent energy-efficiency (EE) gains, validating the complementary benefits of antenna movement, pattern reconfiguration, and tri-hybrid precoding under hardware-inspired power and latency costs.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Bae Jeon, Suhwan Jang, Chan-Byoung Chae

item.title: A Distributed Microphone Network for Real-Time Gunshot Detection and Localization in GNSS-Challenged Large Areas
item.description: arXiv:2611.02591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a scalable distributed acoustic surveillance system for real-time gunshot detection and localiza tion in large-area, GNSS-challenged environments. The system consists of multiple low-cost MEMS microphone array units (MAUs) deployed as distributed anchors. Each MAU performs edge-level sound-event detection using a lightweight Sound De tection and Echo Suppression (SDES) algorithm, followed by a TinyML-based classifier for gunshot identification. For detected gunshots, an enhanced Generalized Cross-Correlation (eGCC) al gorithm estimates intra-array time differences of arrival (TDoAs) with improved robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio and re verberant conditions. Angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimates obtained from individual MAUs are fused through a modified SCO-EV localization framework to determine the gunshot position in a global coordinate system. A misplacement calibration (MC) algorithm compensates for platform orientation errors, improv ing angular consistency and localization accuracy in practical field conditions. Extensive experiments conducted over coverage areas ranging from 4,985 m2 to 49,063 m2 demonstrate reliable operation across varying spatial scales. The proposed framework achieves a Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.70 for gunshot recognition and average localization errors below 6.5 m over 25,000 m2 , while maintaining errors under 15 m at larger scales. The results demonstrate the practical potential of the proposed system for distributed gunshot surveillance in GNSS challenged large areas.
item.dc:creator: Dengke Wang, Bodhibrata Mukhopadhyay, Mohamed-Slim Alouini

item.title: Asymptotic Frequency-Domain FIM for multidimensional stationary and cyclostationary compound-Gaussian processes: Application to DOA estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Whittle formula provides a closed-form expression for the asymptotic Fisher information matrix (FIM) of stationary, zero-mean Gaussian processes (GPs) with finite-dimensional parameterizations, expressed in terms of their power spectra. While this result was recently extended to nonzero-mean, multidimensional, real-valued stationary compound-Gaussian processes (CGPs), its applicability remains limited. In this paper, we significantly broaden this theoretical framework with two primary contributions. First, we extend the Whittle formula to purely cyclostationary real-valued CGPs with parameterized cyclic spectra, and further generalize it to circular and noncircular complex-valued multidimensional stationary CGPs, encompassing both purely and almost cyclostationary CGPs. Second, we apply these novel Whittle-type formulas to evaluate the impact of source spectral characteristics on the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation, particularly in scenarios involving frequency offsets.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Pierre Delmas, Habti Abeida

item.title: How Temporal Dispersion of Radio Channels Depends on Signal Bandwidth
item.description: arXiv:2611.03048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The degree of temporal dispersion of a radio channel is the basis for assessing its transmission capabilities. This paper addresses the practical issue of measuring the temporal parameters of a signal transmitted in the millimeter-wave (38 GHz) range. These parameters provide the basis for assessing the degree of dispersion of the received signal. The measurement results show that both the mean and RMS values of the delay spread depend on the distance between the transmitter and receiver as well as the bandwidth of the transmitted signals. The function description of these relationships (model) is determined based on a statistical analysis of the obtained measurement data obtained in a selected indoor corridor under line-of-sight conditions.
