item.title: Resilient Cell-Free MIMO ISAC Under Uncertainties: An Impairment-Aware Graph Neural Network Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.03054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beamforming designs for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems face the challenge to stay reliable under uncertainties from both channel state information (CSI) as well as clutter. To this end, this paper proposes an impairment-aware heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) framework for beamforming that obtains the CSI error level and the clutter covariance as edge features, which enables a single trained model to adapt to both impairments. In particular, the GNN is trained on a low quantile of the minimum user rate with a clutter-aware signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio, balanced by a normalized Tchebycheff scalarization. Simulation results show that the proposed GNN framework outperforms the considered baselines in sensing-only and communication-only settings. Depending on the operating point, a single GNN model attains approximately 97\% of each baseline's rate while serving both functionalities at once. The model further generalizes to unseen CSI error levels and clutter counts and renders the ISAC system resilient.
item.dc:creator: Oways Alsoloh, Robert-Jeron Reifert, Aymen Khaleel, Stefan Roth, Aydin Sezgin

item.title: Joint Data Association and Tracking for Surveillance Radar Using Gaussian Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing presence of unmanned aerial vehicles or drones has increased the necessity of developing methods to detect and track them to secure restricted airspaces. This can be done using radars which is a common sensor around e.g. airports, an emerging method to track targets is by using Gaussian processes. However, false alarms is ever present in radars especially if tracking weak targets complicating the data association task. We propose a joint data association and tracking algorithm for a single target using a variational Bayesian approach to approximate the full posterior of both the association variable as well as the track. We show that the proposed algorithm outperforms a state of the art data association and tracking algorithm in the form of a Bernoulli filter, as well as the classical Kalman filter, for a large range of detection probabilities.
item.dc:creator: Anders Malthe Westerkam, Troels Pedersen

item.title: Multi-User Precoding with Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces via Neural Reparameterization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) enable wave-domain signal processing, and provide a promising architecture for enhancing spectral efficiency in multi-user wireless communication systems. However, jointly optimizing transmit power and multi-layer phase shifts in SIM-assisted wireless systems under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints results in a large-scale nonconvex problem, for which conventional numerical optimization-based methods, such as alternating optimization (AO), suffer from high computational burden and limited scalability. In this paper, we develop a QoS constraint-aware neural reparameterization framework for SIM-assisted downlink precoding. By embedding the cascaded wave-propagation structure of the SIM into a model-based differentiable architecture, both the phase shift configuration and transmit power allocation are reparameterized as parameters of a structured neural model that inherently satisfies feasibility constraints of the original problem. The resulting formulation enables efficient optimization that does not rely on a channel-to-precoding mapping learned through offline training. Instead, it directly updates the reparameterized optimization variables to realize real-time precoding for any channel realization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior sum rate performance under QoS constraints, while significantly improving computational efficiency compared with conventional numerical optimization approaches.
item.dc:creator: Yongqiang Zhang, Qurrat-Ul-Ain Nadeem

item.title: GIST: Location-Dependent Uplink Path Structure Transfer for FDD Downlink Channel Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A key challenge of downlink (DL) channel estimation in frequency division duplex (FDD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems is the pilot overhead, which grows with the numbers of antennas and subcarriers. However, a prior on path delays and directions shared by the uplink (UL) and DL channels can reduce this overhead. A model trained only on UL channels measured at a base station (BS) can predict the path structure (delays, directions and power gains) from the location of a user equipment (UE) and thereby assist DL channel estimation. In this paper, we propose Gaussian-Informed Structure Transfer (GIST), in which each Gaussian primitive models one propagation path, whose delay, directions and power gain are predicted from the UE location relative to the primitive center. The complex gains of the predicted paths are estimated from DL pilots by linear minimum mean square error estimation with this prior. Experiments on a ray-traced and a measured dataset show that GIST outperforms all baselines, reaching a lower DL estimation error with fewer pilot subcarriers. Further experiments demonstrate its robustness to UE location errors, its low storage and computational requirements.
item.dc:creator: Jinghan Zhang, Xitao Gong, Qi Wang, Mate Boban, Giuseppe Caire

item.title: Single-visit screening for intracochlear tissue growth validated against multi-visit electrical measurement changes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: Tissue growth (TG) around cochlear implant electrodes raises impedance but is not reliably visible on CT scans. Routinely recorded stimulus current-induced non-stimulating electrode voltages (SCINSEVs) carry this information, but a single recording has no patient-specific reference. We present an algorithm for detecting signs of significant TG from a single SCINSEV measurement. Methods: TG is assumed to concentrate basally near the electrode insertion site, leaving the apical region mostly unaffected. A patient-specific forward model built from CT is fitted to the apical measurements and predicts the basal ones. The misfit score, T, measures each basal contact's signed relative misfit against the apical misfit, accounting for apical fit quality and measurement noise. An ear is flagged when two adjacent basal contacts cross a predetermined threshold. We compare T with T-delta, a model-free reference, tracking basal relative to apical SCINSEV change since the intra-operative recording, persisting over the last two visits. Results: T had a false-positive rate of 3% on growth-free ears. It agreed with T-delta in 81% of 68 ears (sensitivity 71%; specificity 86%; p = 6e-6). Over 200 patient-level two-fold splits, median held-out agreement was 78% at a false-positive rate of 5.1%. Conclusion: An apically fitted patient-specific model predicts basal SCINSEVs well enough to flag signs of significant TG at a single visit, without an intra-operative baseline. Detections largely agree with persistent multi-visit basal-versus-apical change, a surrogate ground truth for significant TG.
item.dc:creator: Minh Q. Vu, Erin L. Bratu, Jared A. Rybarczyk, Jack H. Noble

item.title: InSARFlow: Riemannian Flow Matching for Interferometric SAR
item.description: arXiv:2611.00003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) enables the analysis of topological changes in natural sites or urban areas. This technique operates by recovering the surface displacement from the study of the phase difference (interferogram) between two or multiple SAR images of the same scene at different times. In practice, the use of phase denoising algorithms is necessary to extract relevant information from the interferograms, which motivated numerous developments in the past decade. Due to the inherent periodicity of phases, interferograms can naturally be represented as points on a Riemannian manifold (specifically, the flat torus). This strong prior knowledge motivates the design of learning-based methods that respect the interferogram's intrinsic geometric constraints. Building on this observation, this paper introduces InSARFlow: a generative modeling framework for the denoising and generation of interferograms. Unlike conventional deep learning approaches formulated in Euclidean spaces, which may violate phase periodicity and produce invalid estimates, this method leverages Riemannian flow matching to learn distributional transports directly on the torus. The interest of this approach is demonstrated on two use cases: (1) realistic interferogram generation, in which we model the transport between uniform noise on the torus to real-world interferograms; (2) interferogram denoising, where InSARFlow transports noisy interferograms to their denoised counterparts. Extensive experiments on a controlled synthetic dataset validate the effectiveness of InSARFlow for interferogram denoising. The proposed approach consistently outperforms studied baselines, highlighting the benefits of geometry-aware learning on the torus. Code and weights available at https://github.com/lebellig/insarflow.
item.dc:creator: Georges Le Bellier (LIP, OCKHAM, CEDRIC - VERTIGO), Arnaud Breloy (CEDRIC - VERTIGO), Nicolas Audebert (IGN, CEDRIC - VERTIGO, UR-LSTI-ENSMSE)

item.title: Route-Aware EM Surrogate for Automated LC Matching Network Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.00409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proposes an open-source automated LC matching network optimization framework that combines schematic-level design optimization with electromagnetic (EM)-aware post-layout refinement. An ML-based surrogate predicts the frequency-dependent complex admittance of individual routes, enabling reuse across matching network topologies and physical layouts for the same technology node without retraining. These route models guide post-layout passive retuning to recover matching performance while preserving the layout footprint. Evaluated in a commercial 65nm CMOS technology, the surrogate achieves 1.94-4.91% mean absolute percentage error with respect to a full-wave electromagnetic solver, with no detected passivity violations. Across nine LC matching networks operating at 5-95GHz, our framework recovers S_11 from -6.37dB, for schematic-level optimization after post-layout degradation to -22.27dB after EM-aware post-layout refinement. All designs meet matching targets under full-layout EM verification in optimization runtimes below 70s.
item.dc:creator: Subhadip Ghosh, Surya Srikar Peri, Ramesh Harjani, Sachin S. Sapatnekar

item.title: mmWave UE Positioning Under Blockage: Limits for ISAC-Assisted Handover
item.description: arXiv:2611.00453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Proactive handover can save a millimeter-wave (mmWave) link before a passing body blocks it, but only if the network knows where the user is. We ask whether the radio units that serve a user can localize it accurately enough from its uplink sounding reference signals. We derive position error bounds that include synchronization and array calibration errors, with and without reflected paths known from a digital twin, and test two estimators in a ray-traced street canyon on held-out scenarios. Three findings stand out. First, with line of sight to both radio units, array calibration, not bandwidth, limits the bound. Second, blockage degrades the line-of-sight-only bound sharply, whereas known reflections keep the map-aided bound low. Third, a simple dominant-path estimator fails where it matters most: its errors grow sharply around blockage, and proactive handover becomes worse than the 3GPP baseline. A map-aided multipath tracker cuts the median error from 12 to 3.7 cm and removes this significant penalty at link margins of 15 dB and above, but does not yet beat the baseline.
item.dc:creator: Seyed Bagher Hashemi Natanzi, Bo Tang

item.title: When Does Spatial Cooperation Help? Contamination Regimes in Decentralized Online Spectrum Anomaly Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.00532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning-based spectrum monitors adapt online to benign propagation changes, but persistent rogue transmissions can gradually become incorporated into the learned background. Spatially distributed receivers provide additional evidence for detecting such anomalies, while decentralized model mixing can also spread contamination to receivers with clean measurements. We study this tradeoff using a decentralized online learner with sample gating and model sharing. We show that, without defenses, contamination propagation is governed by the occupancy rate and is independent of cross-receiver correlation. In contrast, the benefit of spatial fusion depends strongly on correlation and the detector operating point, so cooperation can either improve or degrade detection. We also show that fragmented transmissions can evade gating based on temporally smoothed statistics. Combining smoothed and per-sample gating substantially improves robustness to such intermittent contamination.
item.dc:creator: Alp Berke Ardic, Erdem Koyuncu

item.title: Communication-Efficient Model-Distributed Inference for CBRS Radar Detection at the Edge
item.description: arXiv:2611.00625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) shares the 3550-3700 MHz band between incumbent radar systems and commercial LTE/5G users, so radar activity must be detected accurately and promptly. Spectrogram-based YOLO detectors can localize coexisting radar and cellular signals, but running them on resource-constrained edge devices is challenging. Model-distributed inference (MDI) can increase throughput by partitioning a model across edge devices. Using an end-to-end pipeline from raw I/Q samples to on-device detection, we show that partitioning recent YOLO generations incurs high activation-transfer costs due to their multi-scale structures. To reduce these costs, we propose CEDAR, a communication-efficient, edge-distributed architecture for radar detection. Its RF-aware detector, CEDAR-YOLO, removes YOLO's multi-scale neck and two of its three detection scales, leaving a single-scale path with independently configured frequency and time resolutions, which lowers the communication cost of partitioning. Its compression-aware MDI framework, CEDAR-MDI, integrates lightweight activation compressors and selects, for each compressor, the partition that minimizes the pipeline bottleneck. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano testbed with real-world over-the-air data, CEDAR-YOLO reduces the parameter count by 35-57% and model inference time by 16-33%, and CEDAR-MDI achieves up to $3.27\times$ the throughput of single-device inference, with detection quality preserved in both cases.
item.dc:creator: Teng Li, Hulya Seferoglu

item.title: From Confounding to Counterfactuals: A Cross-Layer Causal Model for RAN Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2611.00635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data-driven control in radio access networks (RANs) selects resource allocations using associations between control actions and key performance indicators (KPIs) learned from network telemetry. Because the shared radio environment influences both the scheduler's decisions and the resulting performance, a bias known as confounding, such associations overstate the effect of an allocation and misdirect resources toward user equipment (UEs) that cannot benefit. Moreover, individual UEs respond heterogeneously to the same decision, so even a corrected average effect does not identify which UEs gain from additional resources. While causal inference has recently been applied to RANs, existing approaches do not model the cross-layer mechanisms that connect an allocation to its outcome. In this paper, a hierarchical structural causal model (H-SCM) spanning the PHY, MAC, and network layers is proposed that separates cell-load confounding from UE-specific response heterogeneity. In particular, a counterfactual scheduling problem is formulated in which physical resource block (PRB) allocations are selected using per-UE counterfactual goodput rather than observational conditional averages. This problem is solved via a pipeline combining constrained causal discovery, structural-equation fitting, and abduction-action-prediction. Simulations demonstrate that naive observational estimation overstates the full-PRB response by 73.3%, whereas adjustment for cell-load confounding reduces the relative error to 9.8%. Held-out interventions are predicted with a coefficient of determination of 0.988. Counterfactual scheduling achieves a mean relative loss in total cell goodput below 0.5% against the ground-truth optimum, compared with 2.0-2.9% for a neural-network baseline.
item.dc:creator: Artin Elhamirad, Christo Kurisummoottil Thomas, Ali Tajer

item.title: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission
item.description: arXiv:2611.00697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) can correct the residual errors of a standard channel code with a foundation model that supplies a prior on the source content, but existing SECC schemes are designed for text. In this paper, we develop SECC for image transmission with spatial token interleaving and a two-pass belief propagation (BP) schedule. At the transmitter, a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer converts an image into tokens, which are transmitted in multiple low-density parity-check (LDPC) code blocks of fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR). In raster order, a block that BP fails to decode corrupts consecutive token rows, so the interleaver reorders the tokens such that adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks, without additional transmitted bits. At the receiver, after the first BP pass, token recovery fuses the token probabilities given by BP with the predictions of the autoregressive model Emu3-Gen, and the second BP pass decodes each block again with the fused distributions as priors on the information bits. On Kodak24 at 0.5 channel uses per pixel and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 0.15 dB, the second pass removes 92% of the token errors left by token recovery, and interleaving reduces the final token error rate by 88%. At medium to high SNR, the proposed receiver exceeds deep joint source--channel coding baselines with the same channel uses by at least 1.2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Feng, Chentao Yue, Haiyao Yu, Gaoyang Pang, Xinyu Chen, Hao Chang, Branka Vucetic, Yonghui Li

item.title: What matters in classical machine learning for non-intrusive load monitoring? A factorial benchmark on REFIT with validation on unseen houses
item.description: arXiv:2611.00920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Published classical machine-learning results for appliance ON/OFF classification in nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) range from F1-type scores of 0.53 to 0.98, and the sources of this spread have not been separated. This study separates them with a factorial benchmark on REFIT: seven models, two feature sets and four class-imbalance strategies for five appliances (270 fitted configurations), each evaluated by pooled nested cross-validation and on houses unseen during training, with robustness checks. An analysis of variance shows that the appliance explains 38% of the variance in F1, the feature set 13% and the model only 8%. Engineered rolling-window features raised the mean F1 score by 52% under both protocols. Other conclusions changed on unseen houses: the support-weighted F1 score of the best pooled configurations fell from 0.548 to 0.447, the differences between the models selected by pooled validation were no longer significant, and the benefit of class weighting over no correction rose from 32% to 69%. In a nested comparison, house-grouped selection on the training houses improved F1 on unseen houses for three of five appliances, by up to 0.110, and was within 0.007 for the other two. These findings held across four house partitions and without the solar-affected houses. A same-protocol convolutional network reached a weighted F1 score of 0.50, about 0.05 above the classical models (0.45) and far below the published deep-learning scores of 0.78 to 0.91, which were obtained under a different protocol. The results support low-cost appliance monitoring in buildings and yield a NILM reporting checklist.
item.dc:creator: Zablon Ombiro

item.title: Learning Gradients of Homogeneous Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Homogeneous gradient functions have widespread significance, including applications in maximum energy subspace selection and retrieval problems. Euler's homogeneous function theorem specifies how the potential associated with a positively k-homogeneous gradient field can be recovered directly from the field itself. We use Euler's theorem to build on GradNets and propose a homogeneous gradient network architecture that is guaranteed to correspond to the gradient of a homogeneous function. Then, we describe how monotone homogeneous GradNets universally approximate the gradients of k-homogeneous convex functions. The inductive bias of homogeneous GradNets enables them to outperform baseline ICNNs by up to 7dB in our max energy subspace projection experiment and by up to 13% higher accuracy, 98% fewer parameters, and 70% fewer FLOPS in our amortized inner product search experiment.
item.dc:creator: Mayur S. Gowda, Srinivasa Pranav, Shreyas Chaudhari, Jos\'e M. F. Moura

item.title: Secrecy Sum-Rate Maximization for RSMA-Enabled Pinching-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates secrecy sum-rate (SSR) maximization in a downlink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-enabled single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) with an external eavesdropper. The RSMA power allocation, secure common-rate allocation, and pinching-antenna (PA) positions are jointly optimized subject to transmit-power, per-user secrecy-rate, and PA-placement constraints. To tackle the resulting nonconvex problem, an alternating-optimization framework is developed, combining successive convex approximation for RSMA resource allocation with feasibility-preserving projected gradient ascent for PA-position optimization. Numerical results show that the proposed design consistently outperforms the considered benchmarks in terms of average SSR, demonstrating the benefits of joint RSMA resource and PA-position optimization for secure PASS transmission.
item.dc:creator: Code Kebe, Saeid Pakravan, Wessam Ajib

item.title: 6G Uplink Waveform and Rank Selection under Distributed Reception
item.description: arXiv:2611.01590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The development of 6G uplink is expanding waveform and spatial transmission options, while distributed reception makes their relative merits depend on the spatial and frequency structure of the aggregate channel. We study the joint selection of cyclic prefix orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing and discrete Fourier transform spread OFDM at rank 1 and noncoherent rank 2 under common user equipment power constraints and centralized linear minimum mean-square error reception. We derive waveform switching thresholds at both ranks and a rank selection margin, establishing conditions for selecting among the four modes based on available transmit power, DFT despreading loss, and spatial multiplexing gain. We then characterize how port gains and correlations at individual access points (APs) form aggregate spatial separation and influence mode selection. At fixed port gains and available transmit powers, improving spatial separation without reducing it on any subcarrier increases the rank selection margin, while its effect on the preferred waveform within rank 2 depends on the frequency distribution of the improvement. Numerical results show that different AP deployments can favor different waveforms and ranks, even with the same receive antenna budget and comparable aggregate channel gains, including waveform switches at a fixed preferred rank.
item.dc:creator: Yewen Cao, Fen Hou, Yulin Shao

item.title: Worst-User Outage Probability Minimization in Active RIS-Aided Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01650v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, a worst-user outage probability minimization problem in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided systems is addressed. Since the resulting problem involves a discontinuous objective function over an unknown channel distribution, a sequence of reformulations is applied by integrating a probability-simplex user weighting, a softplus surrogate for differentiability, and entropic tail-risk aggregation for rare but severe outage events. Based on the reformulated problem, a data-driven stochastic optimization technique that relies on historical channel samples is adopted to jointly optimize the beamformer and reflection coefficients with projected adaptive moment estimation. Simulation results show advantages of the proposed technique for reliability-oriented active RIS transmission design.
item.dc:creator: Donghwan Shin, Hyeongtaek Lee, Junil Choi

item.title: Interoperability Assessment of Fronthaul and E2 Interfaces for Multi-Vendor Open RAN Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open Radio Access Networks (RANs) aim to transform the existing wireless network architectures by adopting open interfaces, disaggregating and virtualising RAN components, and enabling dynamic control of the system via data-driven methods. To accelerate the development of interoperable RAN solutions, rigorous assessment of Open Fronthaul and E2 interfaces based on O-RAN Alliance Interoperability Testing (IOT) specifications plays a key role as the integration of these interfaces seems to be very challenging, e.g. due to the need for alignment of Fronthaul IOT profiles and unforeseen challenges for E2 interface integration as Near-Real-Time RAN Intelligent Controller (Near-RT RIC) is relatively a new component introduced within the RAN architecture. In this paper, selected parts of the latest findings and lessons learned from interoperability assessment of Open Fronthaul and E2 interfaces for 13 multi-vendor Open RAN systems deployed in SmartRAN Open Network Interoperability Centre (SONIC) Labs are presented.
item.dc:creator: Farhad Mehran, Charles Turyagyenda, Dritan Kaleshi

item.title: Acoustic and Attentional Challenges Shape the Balance Between Attended and Competing Speech Tracking Differently
item.description: arXiv:2611.01876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Selective attention enhances cortical tracking of attended speech, but the role of ignored speech remains less clear. In particular, it is unknown whether attended and ignored speech contribute to cortical tracking in a fixed balance or whether this balance changes with listening conditions. We addressed this question across six electroencephalography (EEG) datasets spanning acoustic and attentional challenges, hearing impairment, and hearing-aid processing. We systematically varied the relative weighting of attended and competing speech and studied how their combined contribution affected cortical speech tracking. Across most listening conditions, cortical tracking was improved when we included competing speech, compared with attended speech alone. Importantly, the balance between attended and competing speech changed across conditions. Increasing acoustic difficulty increased both the benefit and the optimal contribution of competing speech, with the same general pattern observed in normal-hearing and hearing-impaired listeners. In the hearing-aid datasets examining noise-reduction conditions, the contribution of competing speech was more limited. Attentional challenges also changed the contribution of competing speech, but differently from acoustic challenges. These findings show that attended and competing speech do not contribute to cortical tracking in a fixed balance. Rather, their balance depends on the listening challenge. Although these results do not define a single optimal ratio, they provide a step toward hearing devices that adapt not only to the attended talker, but also to how competing speech is balanced in complex listening environments.
item.dc:creator: Johanna Wilroth, Martin A. Skoglund, Emina Alickovic, Martin Enqvist

item.title: ECGJev: Question-Conditioned Option Scoring for 12-Lead ECG Interpretation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical interpretation of a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) often requires answering targeted diagnostic questions with clear, quantifiable decisions. We introduce ECGJev, the first ECG framework built on a decision decoder, a pretrained language model trained to return a probability for every listed option. A question-conditioned bridge compresses frozen waveform and spectrogram features into 16 ECG tokens, and a two-stage procedure adapts the bridge and low-rank adapters on the decoder's native option readout using diagnostic labels alone, scoring all options for a question in one forward pass. Evaluated across four ECG benchmarks, ECGJev achieves the highest macro-F1 on CPSC2018 (80.46%), PTB-XL (71.68%) and Chapman (96.86%), and generalizes competitively to the small-sample PTB cohort. Concept probes and perturbation analyses further show that its predictions rely directly on the ECG input, remain stable under option-order and wording variations, and transfer zero-shot to unseen waveform concepts. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhuoyuanli-lab/ECGJev.
item.dc:creator: Zhuoyuan Li, Xidong Wu, Hanyu Cui, Jiansong Gao, Rongrong Fu, Mingke Yan, Haotian Tang

item.title: Wideband Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) for Frequency-Flat and Frequency-Selective Processing
item.description: arXiv:2611.02109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC) has been proposed as an analog processing architecture to perform efficient computation in the microwave domain. Consisting of reconfigurable impedance networks, a MiLAC can extract many of the gains of large multi-antenna systems without costly digital processing, e.g., achieving capacity in narrowband multiple-input single-output (MISO). However, the behavior of wideband MiLAC, required to support high data-rate transmissions, is widely unknown. The impedance components of MiLACs have non-trivial frequency-dependent response, requiring specific implementations to characterize it. In this work, we consider MiLAC implementations based on LC resonators with tunable capacitance, which allow synthesizing near-arbitrary passive lossless impedance matrices at individual frequencies using inductors and varactors. We characterize the mapping between optimal MISO precoding at a reference frequency, and the vector of capacitances configuring the MiLAC. We derive the degrees of freedom (DoFs) remaining after fixing such optimum precoding at the reference frequency, and show that these DoFs can be exploited to tune the frequency response of the MiLAC. We propose two techniques to exploit these DoFs: a closed-form approach for frequency-flat MiLAC processing, and a numerical approach for multi-frequency MiLAC processing, optimizing processing at frequencies other than the reference one. The frequency-flat approach shows satisfactory performance in a simulated frequency-flat millimeter-wave scenario, approaching the performance of digital processing. The multi-frequency approach can adapt to the frequency-selectivity of a simulated sub-6GHz scenario, attaining gains over frequency-flat digital processing. This constitutes the first demonstration that realistic MiLAC implementations can be configured to perform independent computations at different frequencies.
item.dc:creator: Juan Vidal Alegr\'{i}a, Matteo Nerini, Bruno Clerckx

item.title: Inner-Speech Decoding from EEG Across Three Corpora Under a Fixed Architecture and Protocol
item.description: arXiv:2611.02180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inner-speech decoding from electroencephalography could support non-invasive communication for people with severe motor impairment, but comparison across studies is hindered by dataset- and protocol-specific evaluation. We present a controlled cross-dataset study using one preprocessing pipeline, one within-subject five-fold cross-validation protocol, and a compact dual-attention Transformer (VC-DATNet; approximately 131,000 parameters) across three public corpora: Thinking Out Loud (10 participants), BISpeech (4), and SyncSpeech (3). VC-DATNet achieved per-participant sensor/source hybrid accuracies of 39.48% on the four-class Thinking Out Loud task, 20.60% on the eight-word BISpeech task, and 25.53% on the eight-word SyncSpeech task, for which we report the first decoding result. Sensor-space and cortical source-space representations were complementary, with each performing better for different participants; this pattern replicated across all three corpora and nine architectures. Moreover, ten decoders spanning convolutional, recurrent, temporal-convolutional, hybrid Transformer, and pretrained foundation-model families converged within a narrow accuracy range on every dataset. These findings indicate that representation choice should be individualized and suggest that performance on these public corpora is constrained more by signal quality and dataset scale than by model capacity. The released pipeline provides a reproducible benchmark for future inner-speech decoding studies

item.title: Design and Analysis of Pinching-Antenna Systems With Radially Deployed Waveguides (X-PASS)
item.description: arXiv:2611.02687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide. A single waveguide, however, confines its antennas to one line, so that good coverage of an area has relied on several waveguides or waveguide segments with separate feeds. This paper proposes X-PASS, in which a hub feeds radially deployed waveguide arms, one pinching antenna on each, and drives them by arm selection, aggregation or multiplexing. It models the hub with its insertion losses, derives a unified signal-to-noise ratio expression for these three operating modes, and derives in closed form a radius inside which aggregation outperforms selection. Numerical results validate the analysis and compare the coverage of X-PASS with that of the other layouts at equal transmit power.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jiang, Hans D. Schotten

item.title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Secret Key Generation over Temporally Correlated Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.02761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physical-layer key generation (PLKG) exploits reciprocal channel dynamics to generate symmetric keys, addressing the key distribution problem in wireless communications. However, strong temporal correlation in slow-fading environments limits fresh randomness and results in low key generation rates. Movable antennas (MAs) introduce spatial degrees of freedom through antenna repositioning, providing a new approach to addressing the limitation. This paper investigates MA-assisted PLKG over temporally correlated channels. A first-order Gauss-Markov process is utilized to characterize the temporal correlation of multipath gains. We characterize the full-sequence mutual information (MI) over temporally correlated channels. For fixed antenna positions and beamforming, we establish a finite-horizon approximation error bound that vanishes as both effective signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) increase. We derive a closed-form expression for the one-step conditional MI and adopt it as a tractable key-information metric. A nonconvex problem is formulated to jointly optimize antenna positions and per-slot beamforming under transmit-power and minimum-spacing constraints. We develop an alternating optimization algorithm, combining an exact principal-eigenvector beamforming solution with feasible SCA-based projected gradient position updates. Simulation results demonstrate that the MA-assisted scheme outperforms the fixed-position antenna baseline. At a high temporal correlation coefficient, position optimization achieves approximately $51\%$ higher rates than fixed antennas. Joint position and beamforming optimization provides a further $106\%$ gain over position optimization alone, demonstrating more pronounced gains under strong temporal correlation.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyu Huang, Chen Sun, Guyue Li, Guanghui Wen, Xianbin Wang

item.title: Localization MSE Analysis for Cooperative OFDM-ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2611.02783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper develops a receiver-specific mean-squared-error (MSE) framework for cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) localization using random orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) payloads. It captures local peak perturbations and incorrect ambiguity-peak acquisition for two classical receiver processing schemes: matched filtering (MF) and reciprocal filtering (RF). For scatterers well separated in delay, we quantify how frequency spread and interference induced by symbol-energy fluctuations affect local delay errors under MF. RF removes symbol-dependent weighting but amplifies noise for low-energy symbols. Payload-conditioned joint Gaussian delay profiles yield peak-selection probabilities, which combine with nonlinear multistatic fusion errors to approximate position MSE while accounting for network geometry. Numerical results illustrate receiver-dependent estimation errors and the benefits of frequency-dependent constellation allocation.
item.dc:creator: Kaitao Meng, Kawon Han, Christos Masouros

item.title: Electromagnetic Information Theory for Programmable Metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.02935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable metasurfaces enable fine-grained control of electromagnetic waves and are creating new opportunities for information extraction, information transfer and information processing. Yet, despite exciting experimental demonstrations, their fundamental capabilities remain poorly understood. In this Perspective, we argue that programmable metasurfaces, and programmable wave systems more generally, call for an electromagnetic information theory that addresses limits at two levels, in a unified manner across applications like communications, sensing and computing. First, for a given physical platform, such a theory should bound achievable information manipulations, such as sensing precision, information-transfer rates, and computational performance. Second, at a more fundamental level, it should determine what non-programmable and programmable physical resources bound these system-specific limits, and what minimum resources are required to attain a prescribed level of performance. We discuss emerging theoretical approaches to these questions, and their connection to experimentally realizable systems. We examine how device thickness, programmable degrees of freedom, nonlocality, coupling and multiple scattering constrain these limits. Establishing the envisioned framework could clarify the ultimate capabilities of programmable metasurfaces and guide the design of future wave-based information systems.
item.dc:creator: Philipp del Hougne, Marco Di Renzo, Owen D. Miller, David A. B. Miller

item.title: Leakage-Aware Encrypted Semantic Communication with Key-Conditioned Signal Perturbation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Encrypted semantic communication systems protect transmitted messages by inserting key-conditioned modules into a deep-learning semantic communication pipeline, but existing designs rely on a fixed adversarial weight and operate mainly at the semantic-feature level. We propose two changes to the encrypted semantic communication system (ESCS): a key-conditioned signal-domain perturbation layer, called learned adversarial perturbation injection (LAPI), and an information noise-contrastive estimation (InfoNCE)-guided adaptive training rule that {adds an adaptive leakage penalty alongside the fixed adversarial objective} using an InfoNCE-based proxy for mutual information leakage. Experiments on the Europarl corpus over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Rayleigh fading channels show that InfoNCE-guided training is the primary source of eavesdropper suppression, reducing the eavesdropper's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) score to approximately 0.07 at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Adding LAPI to the InfoNCE-guided objective further lowers the InfoNCE-estimated leakage by 5-9% with low measured inference overhead, while its impact on legitimate-receiver BLEU depends on channel conditions. The two mechanisms operate on different parts of the pipeline and can be jointly applied.
item.dc:creator: Omar Kaaki, Maria Slim, Mariette Awad, Hadi Sarieddeen

item.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Uncoded versus Row-Wise Coded Placements
item.description: arXiv:2611.03045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A\leq K$ users is active in the delivery phase. In all regimes where the optimal hotplug tradeoff is known, it depends only on $A$, not on $K$; whether this holds in general is open. We show that: (i) Under uncoded placement, YMA delivery with MAN placement, where offline users are assigned the demands of active users, is optimal. Hence, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, while the MAN placement is optimal for every number of active users; (ii) Under row-wise placement (RWP), where each cache is a function of the user's own row of each file, every classical scheme can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code. The resulting hotplug scheme has the tradeoff of the classical model with $A$ users, for every $A\leq K$: there is no load penalty, but the placement depends on $K$. We then derive a converse for RWP, which shows that: (a) for $2\leq N\leq A$, the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV) is RWP optimal for $AM\leq N/(N-1)$, which settles the RWP tradeoff for $N=2$; (b) YMA is RWP optimal at $AM=N$; and (c) for $N=A=3$, GV is RWP optimal for $M\leq 1$. Hence, the Reed-Solomon embeddings of these schemes are optimal among embedded RWP schemes.
item.dc:creator: Daniela Tuninetti

item.title: A Tightly Coupled Magnetic-Inertial SLAM System for Field Robots
item.description: arXiv:2611.03106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Field robots operating in mines, tunnels, and disaster areas require reliable localization despite GNSS denial and degraded camera and LiDAR measurements caused by dust, smoke, or poor illumination. Missions involving both ground and aerial robots further motivate complementary sensing modalities that do not depend on visibility, preinstalled infrastructure, or wheel contact. This letter presents MISLAM, a tightly coupled magnetic-inertial simultaneous localization and mapping system using an IMU and a nine-magnetometer array, without relying on external odometry or platform-specific motion assumptions. The system combines the inertial navigation model with local polynomial magnetic-field models for short-term motion estimation and a global Gaussian process model for drift correction using an error-state Kalman filter. Offline evaluation on three indoor datasets collected with a handheld rig shows reductions in total endpoint closure error of 45.7% - 78.0% relative to magnetic-inertial odometry. Under poor illumination, MISLAM maintains tracking after visual-inertial odometry fails, achieving a horizontal closure error of 0.332 m, although vertical drift remains a limitation. These results support magnetic-inertial SLAM as a complementary localization modality for robotic sensor suites operating under degraded visual conditions.
item.dc:creator: Chuan Huang, Tongxing Peng

item.title: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO
item.description: arXiv:2611.03193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This letter investigates a cell-free massive MIMO system with $L$ access points (APs), each employing a small fixed-form-factor, uniform linear array of $N$ potentially closely spaced antennas. Utilizing multiport communication theory, we analyze the impact of mutual coupling on uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) under various impedance-matching strategies. We compare two deployment regimes: ($i$) increasing $N$ while $L$ is kept fixed, and ($ii$) increasing $N$ while fixing the total antenna count $M = NL$. Numerical results show that, with a full matching network, mutual coupling itself becomes beneficial when an AP serves several user equipments, which is the typical operating regime of user-centric cell-free networks. Furthermore, with full matching, antenna densification can enhance SE or allow for a reduction in the number of APs without performance loss. Since full matching networks remain of manageable size in the small arrays of distributed APs, unlike in large centralized arrays, cell-free networks offer a natural setting for exploiting mutual coupling.
item.dc:creator: Erind Tufa, Antonio A. D'Amico, Luca Sanguinetti

item.title: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Distributed Consensus: Algorithm Design and Power Control Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.03378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) aggregation offers a scalable and communication-efficient approach to distributed average consensus in wireless networks, without requiring instantaneous channel state information (CSI) or phase alignment. However, persistent aggregation errors pose fundamental challenges in achieving exact average consensus under nominal distributed averaging protocols. In this paper, we develop an NCOTA consensus framework that accommodates row-stochastic mixing, without requiring the conventional average-preservation property of doubly stochastic mixing matrices. Building on a distributed optimization formulation of average consensus, we propose a decentralized projected gradient descent with row-stochastic mixing (DPGD-RS) algorithm and establish its mean-square convergence to the exact average of the agents' initial states. We further derive a closed-form upper bound on the mean-square consensus error, characterizing the effects of aggregation uncertainty, network connectivity, and mixing imbalance. Guided by this analysis, we propose a spectral-reshaping power control (SR-PC) scheme that jointly optimizes transmit powers and receive-scaling factors to accelerate convergence by balancing aggregation accuracy and network mixing. Numerical results validate the theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrate that the proposed power control scheme significantly accelerates convergence compared with full-power transmission and spectral-radius-minimization benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Yuhang Deng, Zheng Chen, Erik G. Larsson

item.title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.03512v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. We split this spectral shift into an operator channel and a frequency channel, each with a dimensionless measure. ST-GFM (Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting Model) filters every input step with Chebyshev and bidirectional diffusion filters on one learned, non-symmetric operator and alternates them with per-node temporal attention. For the operator channel we prove Frobenius-norm perturbation bounds for both graph branches, show that the Chebyshev bound is attained to first order, and compute its constant from the trained weights and the measured operator norm: 17.9 on METR-LA and 21.5 on PEMS-BAY. Under random edge dropout the trained layer moves by 2.0% to 3.1% of this bound. Masked Spectral Reconstruction (MSR), a self-supervised loss active in the first 40 epochs, matches the log power spectrum of the encoder output to that of the input. For small log-spectral residuals on unclamped bins it is proportional to an Itakura-Saito divergence to leading order. Removing it raises the 60-minute MAE by 0.30 on METR-LA, close to the 0.33 lost when all three self-supervised losses go. Under one shared evaluation pipeline, the 60-minute MAE of ST-GFM is 3.5% below a retrained STAEformer on METR-LA and 13.0% below it on PEMS-BAY. Its 60-minute MAE is 3.0980.017 on METR-LA (five seeds) and 1.5760.006 on PEMS-BAY (three seeds), the lowest PEMS-BAY MAE among twelve published baselines.
item.dc:creator: Aashish Bohra, Vivek Vijay

item.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
item.description: arXiv:2611.03558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Nomeir, Sennur Ulukus

item.title: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
item.description: arXiv:2611.03623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Communication is important for our well-being, but it can be impaired by disabilities, such as locked-in syndrome (LIS), cerebral palsy (CP), and dysarthria. Non-invasive brain-to-text brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer a promising solution by providing an alternative communication pathway for people with communication disabilities. However, most recent breakthroughs have relied on large, cumbersome, and costly neuroimaging modalities, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). Numerous studies have attempted decoding using the lighter and cheaper electroencephalography (EEG), but the results remain inferior compared to the other modalities. More importantly, we do not understand how these modalities are related to text at the letter, word, sentence, and higher semantic levels. Many prior studies have focused on decoding below the sentence level because it is considerably easier to design an experiment around phonemes, letters, and words. However, during communication, sentences play a much more important role than words and letters. This is because sentences carry information at such a high level that they can be understood even if some words and letters are missing. However, within sentence-level decoding, sentence classification is not as well investigated as sentence generation, making it difficult to decide whether a sentence should be retrieved or generated in the context of EEG-to-text decoding. This paper strives to investigate sentence-level EEG-to-text classification via a novel hierarchical alignment framework, where the main goal is to retrieve a read sentence using its context and EEG as inputs.
item.dc:creator: Xiaopeng Mao, Morten M{\o}rup, Xin Xu, Sang Wan Lee, Sadasivan Puthusserypady

item.title: HoloTrace: a Location Privacy-Preserving Framework for mmWave MIMO-OFDM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.23444v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-resolution radio localization is becoming increasingly important for next-generation vehicular and mobile networks, enabling infrastructure-assisted positioning for connected and automated mobility. However, the same mmWave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) links used for communication may allow a serving base station (BS) to infer the location of a vehicle-mounted or mobile user equipment (UE) from routine uplink pilot transmissions, even without an explicit positioning request. This paper introduces HoloTrace, a signal-level location-privacy framework for single-BS localization in mmWave MIMO-OFDM systems. HoloTrace modifies user-side pilot symbols while keeping the analog precoder fixed to bias localization-relevant channel features, including angle of arrival (AoA), angle of departure (AoD), and time difference of arrival (TDoA), toward a prescribed fictitious geometry. We formulate pilot-level spoofing as a subspace projection-based signal design problem and derive closed-form oracle designs assuming UE-side channel-gain knowledge. We further develop blind designs that operate without complex path-gain information, while relying on geometric side information, and explicitly characterize their limitations in multipath scenarios. Simulation results with a two-path single-anchor geometry show that oracle HoloTrace can steer the inferred position toward a desired spoofed location, whereas blind variants mainly provide obfuscation or approximate spoofing due to angle-delay pairing ambiguities. The communication impact is geometry-dependent rather than intrinsic to the proposed method: selecting a spoofed location compatible with the serving beams can preserve channel-rate quality while providing effective location privacy.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Italiano, Alireza Pourafzal, Hui Chen, Mattia Brambilla, Gonzalo Seco-Granados, Monica Nicoli, Henk Wymeersch

item.title: Joint Communications, Sensing, and Positioning in 6G Multi-Functional Satellite Systems: Survey and Open Challenges
item.description: arXiv:2509.25937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Satellite systems are expected to be a cornerstone of sixth-generation (6G) networks, supporting communications, sensing, and positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) with global coverage. This survey develops a framework for multi-functional satellite systems (MFSS), which combine at least two of these services through shared or jointly designed payload resources. A two-dimensional taxonomy distinguishes the functional configuration---joint communications and sensing (JCAS), joint communications and PNT (JCAP), joint sensing and PNT (JSAP), or joint communications, sensing, and PNT (JCSAP)---from the integration depth---cooperative, integrated, or joint. After consolidating the communication, sensing, and PNT fundamentals and payload architectures into a single background section, the survey examines the three integration levels and then devotes a dedicated section to each configuration, covering its architecture, classification, state of the art, advantages, key challenges, and research directions. The achievable performance of each configuration is illustrated with representative trade-off results from the literature and compared across configurations, the differences between terrestrial multi-functional networks and satellite MFSS are made explicit, and a life-cycle techno-economic framework balances hardware, spectrum, launch, and operational reuse against engineering, qualification, verification, and common-mode risks. The analysis shows that deeper integration can improve resource utilization and functional synergy, but is not automatically the technical or economic optimum for every mission.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Kumar Sheemar, Jorge Querol, Wali Ullah Khan, Prabhu Thiruvasagam, Sourabh Solanki, Idir Edjekouane, Alejandro Gonzalez-Garrido, Mohammed Al-Ansi, Carla E. Garcia, Symeon Chatzinotas

item.title: Cramer-Rao Bounds for Target Parameter Estimation in a Bi-Static IRS-Assisted Radar Configuration
item.description: arXiv:2603.01660v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The use of Intelligent Reflective Surfaces (IRS) to assist communication and sensing has proven cost-effective in challenging scenarios. For sensing, IRS is shown to sense non-line-of-sight (NLOS) and stealth targets, albeit with significant loss due to the four-hop path model. Amongst the available IRS-assisted configurations, we consider a three-hop model in which the IRS redirects the scattered target response towards the mono-static radar. With the IRS spatially displaced from the radar, this configuration mimics a bi-static radar. While target detection has been studied in this configuration, parameter estimation has not been investigated to date. To this end, we first develop the signal model for this configuration and derive the Cramer Rao Bounds (CRB) for target parameters. The dependence of CRB on system parameters such as SNR, number of snapshots, number of IRS elements and their weights is brought forward through extensive simulations. This study can enable a designer to customize the system parameters to meet the requirements. It also serves as a benchmark for parameter estimation techniques developed for this configuration.
item.dc:creator: S Sanjeeva Reddy, Vinod Veera Reddy

item.title: A Survey on Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces: Fundamentals, Recent Advances, and Challenges
item.description: arXiv:2603.05633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade several closely spaced programmable metasurface layers so that an electromagnetic wave undergoes repeated modulation-propagation interactions before leaving the stack. The stack thereby implements, at the speed of propagation and with few radio-frequency chains, high-dimensional analog transformations that would otherwise require digital precoding, combining, spatial filtering, focusing, or inference. Since 2023, SIM research has produced more than two hundred articles, a dedicated magazine special issue, and two survey-level overviews organized around applications and wave-domain computing. This article complements them with a model-to-hardware perspective. First, we present the electromagnetic modeling hierarchy of SIMs, making explicit the assumptions under which the models coincide, their validity regimes, and their computational complexity, with a common notation for hardware non-idealities and power consumption. Second, we present a methodology-first taxonomy (SIM-aware channel acquisition, model-based optimization, statistical-CSI design, learning-based control, and hardware-aware robust design), compare the families in terms of CSI requirements, complexity, convergence, and hardware constraints, and reconcile conflicting findings in the literature. Third, we synthesize applications by the physical role of the SIM. Fourth, we quantitatively compare experimentally demonstrated multilayer prototypes, separate validated from conceptual architectures, and discuss thermal, tolerance, and calibration issues. Fifth, we provide a tutorial-style performance and trade-off analysis anchored in reported results. Finally, we map evidence-based challenges to research directions with measurable targets. Lessons learned are summarized at the end of every section.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Kumar Sheemar, Sourabh Solanki, Wali Ullah Khan, George C. Alexandropoulos, Symeon Chatzinotas

item.title: Energy-Efficient Velocity Profile Optimization for Movable Antenna-Enabled Sensing Systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.27540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) enable the reconfiguration of array geometry within a bounded region to exploit sub-wavelength spatial degrees of freedom in wireless communication and sensing systems. However, most prior research has predominantly focused on the communication and sensing performance, overlooking the mechanical power consumption inherent in antenna movement. To bridge this gap, this paper investigates a velocity profile optimization framework for MA-assisted direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation, explicitly balancing sensing accuracy with mechanical energy consumption of MAs. We first establish a Newtonian-based mechanical energy model, and formulate a functional optimization problem for sensing energy efficiency (EE) maximization. By applying the calculus of variations, this formulation is transformed into an infinite-dimensional problem defined by the Euler-Lagrange equation. To solve it, we propose a spectral discretization framework based on the Galerkin method, which expands the velocity profile over a sinusoidal basis. In the regime where energy consumption is dominated by linear damping, we prove that the optimal velocity profile follows a closed-form sinusoidal shape. For more general scenarios involving strong nonlinear aerodynamic drag, we leverage the Markov-Luk\'{a}cs theorem to transform the kinematic constraints into strictly convex sum-of-squares (SOS) conditions. Consequently, the infinite-dimensional problem is reformulated as a tractable finite-dimensional nonlinear algebraic system, which is solved by a two-layer algorithm combining Dinkelbach's method with successive convex approximation (SCA). Numerical results demonstrate that our optimized velocity profile significantly outperforms baselines in terms of EE across various system configurations. Insights into the optimized velocity profiles and practical design guidelines are also provided.
item.dc:creator: Jiannan Wang, Yuyi Mao, Xianghao Yu, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang

item.title: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Discrete Activation based NOMA-assisted Pinching-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.24985v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pinching-antenna systems are a promising architecture for flexible wireless communications, but energy efficiency (EE) maximization remains largely unexplored, as limited existing studies mainly focus on transmit power minimization. This paper investigates EE maximization in a downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-assisted PASS by explicitly modeling the pinching antenna (PA) activation power and jointly optimizing discrete PA activation and power allocation under both quality-of-service and transmit power constraints. To tackle the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem, a two-layer iterative algorithm is proposed with an EE-oriented matching-based PA activation and a Dinkelbach-based power allocation with closed-form updates. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution achieves substantial EE gains over the considered benchmark schemes, while exhibiting fast convergence. The impact of activation power has been analyzed and the significance of accounting it in EE maximization problem is also demonstrated.
item.dc:creator: Yishi Zhang, Aditya Powari, Kaidi Wang, Yaru Fu, Daniel K. C. So

item.title: Octree-Context Gaussian Splatting with Multi-Order Propagation for Channel Knowledge Maps
item.description: arXiv:2605.22961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) can support environment-aware wireless communications by providing site-specific channel knowledge as a function of the transmitter position, the receiver position or both. Existing Gaussian splatting CKM methods can reduce the high training and inference costs of implicit neural methods yet represent all multipath interactions by one wireless radiance field. We propose octree-context Gaussian splatting (OctCGS), which anchors Gaussian primitives on an octree as virtual scattering nodes and decomposes multi-bounce propagation into orders by the number of node-level interactions along each path. Shared tree attention gives each node local context from neighboring octree cells and room-wide context from ancestor cells at a cost linear in the number of cells, and the order-wise scattering of each node is predicted from this context. The order-wise contributions of the power transported between the nodes are summed in power with a line-of-sight (LoS) term to give the channel gain and the spatial spectrum. OctCGS raises the spatial-spectrum structural similarity (SSIM) by 0.13 to 0.23 and lowers the mean absolute error (MAE) of the channel gain by 0.9 to 3.8 dB on five indoor ray-tracing scenes, relative to the best baseline per scene and metric.
item.dc:creator: Jinghan Zhang, Xitao Gong, Qi Wang, Richard A. Stirling-Gallacher, Giuseppe Caire

item.title: Vertical Pinching Antenna Systems (V-PAS) Aided UAV Communications
item.description: arXiv:2607.23184v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To address the limitation that existing horizontal pinching antenna systems (H-PAS) are primarily designed for ground users and confined to two-dimensional (2D) coverage, this paper proposes deploying a pinching antenna (PA) along the facade of urban buildings to construct a vertical pinching antenna system (V-PAS) for ultra-low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications. The proposed architecture employs a dielectric waveguide continuously deployed along the full height of buildings, extending the considered user service region of PAS from a 2D ground plane to a three-dimensional (3D) low-altitude airspace, enabling stable line-of-sight (LoS) links for "last meter" UAV communications. We define the concept of pinching multiplicative path loss (PMPL) to characterize the cascaded multiplicative attenuation of the waveguide and free-space path losses. It is found that PMPL is insensitive to vertical distance, rendering V-PAS highly adaptive to building heights. Furthermore, accurate and asymptotic closed-form expressions for outage probability and ergodic rate under lossy waveguide conditions are derived, respectively. The optimal access point (AP) height and PA position are further characterized, providing deployment insights for practical V-PAS. The results show that V-PAS achieves performance advantages over H-PAS and the benchmark without PA in most ultra-low-altitude UAV communication scenarios. Only under extremely high transmission power and large UAV operational area may the outage probability of V-PAS with a lossy waveguide be inferior to that of the benchmark without PA, but the ergodic rate of V-PAS still maintains an advantage. By contrast, V-PAS with a lossless waveguide outperforms the benchmark without PA in UAV communications, representing the theoretical performance upper bound of V-PAS.
item.dc:creator: Tao Wang, Kunrui Cao, Yayun Qu, Lu Lv, Xianfu Lei, Dimitrios Tyrovolas, Panagiotis D. Diamantoulakis

item.title: Antenna Positioning and Beamforming Optimization in MA Enabled Secure ISAC Systems: A Gradient-Based Meta Learning Approach
item.description: arXiv:2608.12870v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) significantly improves spectral efficiency but introduces security risks regarding the interception of embedded communication signals. This paper proposes an movable antenna (MA)-enabled secure ISAC system that utilizes the spatial degrees of freedom of MA to mitigate these risks. Then, a problem is formulated to maximize the system secrecy rate by jointly optimizing antenna positioning, transmit beamforming, and artificial noise. However, the principal challenge arises from the non-convexity of the optimization problem and the strong coupling of the optimization variables. Generally, traditional optimization methods for this problem suffer from complex mathematical derivations, while existing deep learning approaches rely heavily on the training data distribution. To address these issues, we introduce a gradient-based meta learning (GML) algorithm, which works without pre-training and demonstrates favorable performance. Specifically, the algorithm establishes a neural network for each optimization variable, where the gradient of the objective function with respect to the variable serves as the input, and the output of the network determines the variable's update step. By handling the constraints and constructing penalty terms, the global loss function is used to guide the optimization process. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves satisfactory performance in terms of both communication security and sensing capabilities.
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Li, Yujie Zhao, Zhou Su, Xiao Tang, Zhiqing Wei, Ying Wang, Wen Chen

item.title: Utility-Aware Adaptive Downlink DM-RS Allocation from Uplink CSI for Lightweight O-DU dApps
item.description: arXiv:2609.22270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Adaptive demodulation reference signal (DM-RS) placement in 5G New Radio (NR) trades pilot overhead against channel-tracking robustness, making a single static density suboptimal across heterogeneous mobility and propagation regimes. This paper studies a lightweight per-UE controller intended for O-DU-side distributed application (dApp) execution. The controller consumes eleven deployable uplink-CSI statistics and selects among six standards-derived PDSCH DM-RS configurations. Rather than optimize oracle-class accuracy, we train an 11-128-64-32-6 multilayer perceptron with a utility-aware objective that preserves the throughput structure of all candidate actions. In a large-scale trajectory-disjoint evaluation covering 294 channel/speed/SNR conditions and 7,056 observations, the proposed U-SoftCE policy significantly improves throughput over a training-selected best fixed pattern by 1.30, 0.86, and 1.13 percentage points on in-distribution, CDL channel-OOD, and 300-km/h mobility-OOD splits, respectively; paired 95% bootstrap intervals exclude zero in all three cases. An independent bit-accurate Sionna NR LDPC validation over 36 held-out conditions and 50 transport blocks per candidate retains a +1.21-point gain with a 95% cluster-bootstrap interval of [0.27, 2.13]. A native C++ implementation uses 12,070 dense parameters and requires 5.59 microseconds mean inference time, while a FlexRIC-based emulated O-DU prototype demonstrates sub-10-ms closed-loop operation. These results support utility-aware objectives for compact adaptive PHY controllers while exposing the limits of exact class-accuracy optimization.

item.title: AVSG: Accelerated Vectorized Sparse Gather for Efficient KV Cache Offload in Sparse-Attention LLM Serving
item.description: arXiv:2609.37538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dynamic sparse attention reduces long-context attention computation by selecting only a subset of tokens, but still requires access to the full KV cache, leaving serving memory-bound. Offloading the KV cache to host memory reduces device memory pressure but places H2D transfers on the decoding critical path. In DSA, substantial overlap in selected KV entries across decoding steps creates an opportunity for device-resident reuse. Exploiting this reuse efficiently, however, presents three critical challenges: costly matching of selected tokens against entries retained in the HBM buffer, uneven distribution of the remaining H2D transfers across accelerator cores, and retaining frequently accessed KV entries within limited HBM capacity. We present AVSG, an operator that addresses these challenges for DSA while preserving its exact token selections. AVSG uses vectorized hash matching to identify reusable HBM-buffer slots and reserve slots for entries requiring transfer, then evenly partitions these H2D transfers across accelerator cores. Lifetime-based buffer management retains frequently accessed KV entries in the device buffer across decoding steps, and shared slot reservations extend reuse across tokens within a multi-token prediction iteration. On a single NPU, vectorized hash matching is 2.80x faster than scalar dual-pointer matching, miss-only transfer raises effective H2D bandwidth by up to 34.44x over request-level assignment, and an 8K-entry buffer reaches a 94.83% hit rate on real requests. These gains translate into end-to-end improvement: on a serving stack processing a real-world production dataset, AVSG reduces time per output token by 39% and increases output throughput by 1.27x relative to the same KV offload layout without HBM-buffer reuse. The code of AVSG is released at https://gitcode.com/cann/cann-recipes-infer.

item.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable-Antenna Compensation of Channel Aging in Over-the-Air Split Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.23118v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Split learning (SL) trains a neural network across devices by exchanging intermediate activations and gradients. In over-the-air SL, the wireless channel serves as an inter-layer linear map, and when the forward and backward channels match, reciprocity and conjugation supply the backward product without channel estimation at the base station (BS). Passive user motion, which the learning link does not control, breaks this match. Movable antennas let the antenna move relative to the user device, and we use this freedom to compensate the displacement. For a stationary BS and a propagation environment quasi-static within each exchange, returning the antenna to its forward-transmission position restores the channel and yields a conditionally unbiased gradient estimate. We also derive when discrete positioning or mechanical movement can achieve this in time. A residual displacement below a quarter wavelength keeps the real part of the channel correlation positive for any angular spectrum. At zero effective offset, independent Gaussian jitter attenuates this correlation without reversing its sign, whereas a persistent offset can reverse it, and in arrays the tolerance depends on the receive-combining direction. These effects enter a nonconvex convergence bound, and a local analysis shows that partial mechanical compensation saves cycle time to first order at only a second-order loss in correlation. In CIFAR-10 experiments, a user terminal without channel state information stays at chance level under uncompensated walking motion, while discrete positioning stays within about 0.3 percentage points of exact restoration, including at a speed beyond the modeled actuator's limit.

item.title: Pilot Decontamination via Data-aided Channel Tracking in Cell-free Massive MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2610.29883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As cell-free massive MIMO emerges as a promising technology for future wireless networks, robust channel estimation becomes increasingly important. Channel estimation relies on pilot transmissions, and with increasing number of users, pilot reuse inevitably introduces contamination that degrades channel estimation and symbol detection. This limitation is compounded by rapidly evolving channels, which render the estimates obsolete over time. To address both the problems, viz. pilot contamination and channel aging without additional pilot overhead, we propose a Kalman filter-based data-aided channel tracking strategy. By leveraging the symbol estimates as virtual pilots, the proposed approach successively refines the channel estimates over time. Unlike the conventional Kalman filter model, here, the observation model depends on symbol estimates, introducing symbol uncertainty that gets coupled with channel uncertainty. This requires a careful calculation of the innovation covariance matrices. Additionally, we discuss a stochastic-gradient-descent based tracking approach with low computational complexity. Extensive simulations are used to demonstrate that successive refinement progressively decontaminates the channel estimate, achieving lower channel estimation error and improved spectral efficiency.

item.title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32889v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Power Amplifier (PA) of a base station operates inefficiently at partial load, where back-off from the peak output power wastes supply headroom. Adapting the PA drain voltage to the instantaneous signal recovers this loss but requires frequent switching, increasing hardware cost. We propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation (TDD-DVM), a drain voltage modulation scheme that instead selects the drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex (TDD) period based on the downlink resource load and switches the voltage during the uplink window. This is enabled by the authors' previous work on POLITE link adaptation, which spreads the transmit power over resources left unused at partial load and moves the PA into a regime where a lower drain voltage suffices. In a 3GPP Urban Macro system-level simulation across traffic loads, we compare TDD-DVM against baseline approaches under conventional and POLITE link adaptation. At equal delivered throughput, TDD-DVM with POLITE keeps the packet failure ratio of the full drain voltage while consuming up to 35% less power than it under conventional link adaptation and up to 7% less than it under POLITE, capturing most of the gain of an idealized reference at moderate loads and roughly half at the highest load.

item.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2610.39110v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.
